191:   if (result == -ETIMEDOUT || result == -ECONNRESET)
192:     {
193:       g_uart.peer_rts_known = false;
194:       g_uart.state_pending = true;
195:     }
196: 
197:   if (command == BK7258_MB_UART_DATA && g_uart.tx_inflight != 0)
198:     {
199:       if (!failed)
200:         {
201:           g_uart.tx_read = (g_uart.tx_read + g_uart.tx_inflight) %
202:                            MB_UART_TX_SIZE;
203:           g_uart.tx_retry_count = 0;
204:         }
205:       else if (result == -ETIMEDOUT || result == -ECONNRESET)
206:         {
207:           /* A failed/unknown ACK cannot tell whether CP consumed the bytes.
208:            * Drop this local chunk rather than replaying terminal characters.
209:            */
210: 
211:           g_uart.tx_read = (g_uart.tx_read + g_uart.tx_inflight) %
212:                            MB_UART_TX_SIZE;
213:           g_uart.stats.tx_unknown++;
214:           g_uart.tx_retry_count = 0;
215:           g_uart.stats.resets++;
216:         }
217:       else
218:         {
219:           g_uart.stats.remote_fail++;
220:           g_uart.state_pending = true;
221:           if (g_uart.tx_retry_count == 0)
222:             {
223:               /* Keep tx_read unchanged.  The same chunk may be copied again
224:                * once STATE recovery succeeds, but only once.
225:                */
226: 
227:               g_uart.tx_retry_count = 1;
228:               g_uart.stats.tx_retry++;
229:             }
230:           else
231:             {
232:               g_uart.tx_read = (g_uart.tx_read + g_uart.tx_inflight) %
233:                                MB_UART_TX_SIZE;
234:               g_uart.tx_retry_count = 0;
235:               g_uart.stats.tx_retry_drop++;
236:             }
237:         }
238: 
239:       g_uart.tx_inflight = 0;
240:     }
241:   else if (command == BK7258_MB_UART_STATE && failed)
242:     {
243:       g_uart.stats.remote_fail++;
244:       /* The transport invokes this completion before it changes READY to
245:        * ABORTING.  Always retain a STATE request so RESET recovery has a
246:        * probe to send after it reaches PROBING.
247:        */
248: 
249:       g_uart.state_pending = true;
250:     }
251: 
252:   g_uart.transaction_busy = false;
253:   nxsem_post(&g_uart.worker_sem);
254: }

256: static int mb_uart_receive(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message,
257:                            uint8_t *ack_flags, void *arg)
258: {
259:   uint8_t command = bk7258_mb_header_cmd(message);
260:   uint16_t length = message->payload_length;
261:   uint16_t first;
262:   bool failed = false;
263:   bool malformed = false;
264: 
265:   (void)arg;
266:   if (ack_flags == NULL)
267:     {
268:       return -EINVAL;
269:     }
270: 
271:   if (command != BK7258_MB_UART_DATA && command != BK7258_MB_UART_STATE)
272:     {
273:       g_uart.stats.bad_flags++;
274:       failed = true;
275:       malformed = true;
276:     }
277:   else if ((message->flags & ~1u) != 0)
278:     {
279:       g_uart.stats.bad_flags++;
280:       failed = true;
281:       malformed = true;
282:     }
283:   else if (message->crc8 != 0)
284:     {
285:       g_uart.stats.bad_crc++;
286:       g_uart.sticky_status |= MB_UART_STATUS_PARITY;
287:       failed = true;
288:       malformed = true;
289:     }
290:   else if (message->reserved != 0)
291:     {
292:       g_uart.stats.bad_reserved++;
293:       failed = true;
294:       malformed = true;
295:     }
296: 
297:   if (!failed && command == BK7258_MB_UART_DATA)
298:     {
299:       if (message->payload_address != BK7258_MB_UART_RX_ADDRESS)
300:         {
301:           g_uart.stats.bad_pointer++;
302:           failed = true;
303:           malformed = true;
304:         }
305:       else if (length == 0 || length > BK7258_MB_UART_CHUNK_SIZE)
306:         {
307:           g_uart.stats.bad_length++;
308:           failed = true;
309:           malformed = true;
310:         }
311:       else if (!bk7258_mailbox_link_ready())
312:         {
313:           failed = true;
314:         }
315:       else if (rx_free() < length)
316:         {
317:           g_uart.stats.rx_overflow++;
318:           g_uart.sticky_status |= MB_UART_STATUS_OVF;
319:           failed = true;
320:         }
321:       else
322:         {
323:           const uint8_t *source =
324:             (const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)BK7258_MB_UART_RX_ADDRESS;
325: 
326:           __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
327:           first = MB_UART_RX_SIZE - g_uart.rx_write;
328:           if (first > length)
329:             {
330:               first = length;
331:             }
332: 
333:           memcpy(&g_uart.rx_ring[g_uart.rx_write], source, first);
334:           if (first != length)
335:             {
336:               memcpy(g_uart.rx_ring, source + first, length - first);
337:             }
338: 
339:           g_uart.rx_write = (g_uart.rx_write + length) % MB_UART_RX_SIZE;
340:           g_uart.stats.data_rx++;
341:           g_uart.stats.rx_bytes += length;
342:         }
343:     }
344:   else if (!failed)
345:     {
346:       if (message->payload_address != 0 || message->payload_length != 0)
347:         {
348:           g_uart.stats.bad_length++;
349:           failed = true;
350:           malformed = true;
351:         }
352:       else
353:         {
354:           g_uart.stats.state_rx++;
355:         }
356:     }
357: 
358:   if (!malformed)
359:     {
360:       bool old_peer_rts = g_uart.peer_rts;
361: 
362:       g_uart.peer_rts = (message->flags & 1u) != 0;
363:       g_uart.peer_rts_known = true;
364:       if (old_peer_rts && !g_uart.peer_rts)
365:         {
366:           nxsem_post(&g_uart.worker_sem);
367:         }
368:     }
369: 
370:   update_local_rts();
371:   *ack_flags = (g_uart.local_rts ? 1u : 0u) | (failed ? 2u : 0u);
372:   nxsem_post(&g_uart.worker_sem);
373:   return malformed ? -EPROTO : OK;
374: }

24: #define BK7258_SYSTICK_RELOAD \
25:   ((CONFIG_BK7258_CPU_FREQ_HZ / TICK_PER_SEC) - 1u)
26: 
27: #if CONFIG_BK7258_CPU_FREQ_HZ % TICK_PER_SEC != 0
28: #  error "BK7258 CPU frequency must divide evenly into the system tick rate"
29: #endif
30: 
31: #if BK7258_SYSTICK_RELOAD > NVIC_MAX_SYSTICK_CNT
32: #  error "BK7258 SysTick reload exceeds the 24-bit counter"
33: #endif
34: 
35: static bool g_first_tick_complete;
36: static uint32_t g_tick_count;
37: 
38: static int bk7258_timerisr(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
39: {
40:   uint32_t tick = ++g_tick_count;
41:   bool first_tick = !g_first_tick_complete;
42: 
43:   (void)irq;
44:   (void)context;
45:   (void)arg;
46: 
47:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(3, (tick << 8) | 1u);
48: 
49:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(3, (tick << 8) | 2u);
50:   nxsched_process_timer();
51:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(3, (tick << 8) | 3u);
52: 
53:   if (first_tick)
54:     {
55:       g_first_tick_complete = true;
56:     }
57: 
58:   return OK;
59: }
60: 
61: int bk7258_timer_start(void)
62: {
63:   if (up_cpu_index() != 0)
64:     {
65:       return -EXDEV;
66:     }
67: 
68:   putreg32(0, NVIC_SYSTICK_CURRENT);
69:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_SYSTICK_STARTED);
70:   putreg32(NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL_CLKSOURCE | NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL_TICKINT |
71:            NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL_ENABLE, NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL);
72:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_SYSTICK);
73:   return OK;
74: }
75: 
76: void up_timer_initialize(void)
77: {
78:   uint32_t priority;
79: 
80:   /* Match the vendor SMP port's configTICK_CORE contract: only logical CPU0
81:    * owns the global tick.  CPU1 leaves its private SysTick disabled.
82:    */
83: 
84:   DEBUGASSERT(up_cpu_index() == 0);
85: 
86:   priority = getreg32(NVIC_SYSH12_15_PRIORITY);
87:   priority &= ~NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_PR15_MASK;
88:   priority |= NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_DEFAULT <<
89:               NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_PR15_SHIFT;
90:   putreg32(priority, NVIC_SYSH12_15_PRIORITY);
91: 
92:   putreg32(0, NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL);
93:   putreg32(BK7258_SYSTICK_RELOAD, NVIC_SYSTICK_RELOAD);
94:   putreg32(0, NVIC_SYSTICK_CURRENT);
95: 
96:   if (irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_SYSTICK, bk7258_timerisr, NULL) < 0)
97:     {
98:       PANIC();
99:     }
100: 
101:   /* nx_start() initializes the clock before nx_smp_start().  Keep SysTick
102:    * stopped until up_cpu_start() has completed the secondary boot transaction.
103:    */
104: }

176:          polls++ < MB_SECONDARY_READY_POLLS)
177:     {
178:       __asm__ volatile("nop");
179:     }
180: 
181:   if (!bk7258_smp_secondary_is_ready())
182:     {
183:       return -ETIMEDOUT;
184:     }
185: #endif
186: 
187:   return OK;
188: }

261: static int send_slot(struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message,
262:                      uint32_t *order)
263: {
264:   uint32_t wire[2];
265:   int ret;
266: 
267:   *order = ++g_send_order;
268:   wire[0] = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)message;
269:   wire[1] = sizeof(*message);
270:   __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
271:   ret = bk7258_mbox_send(0, wire);
272:   if (ret == OK)
273:     {
274:       g_stats.tx++;
275:     }
276:   else if (ret == -EAGAIN)
277:     {
278:       g_stats.fifo_full++;
279:     }
280: 
281:   if (ret < 0)
282:     {
283:       g_stats.last_tx_error = (uint32_t)(-ret);
284:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(3,
285:         (g_stats.last_tx_error & 0xffu) |
286:         ((g_stats.timeout & 0xffu) << 8) |
287:         ((g_stats.fifo_full & 0xffu) << 16) |
288:         ((g_stats.ack_overflow & 0xffu) << 24));
289:     }
290: 
291:   return ret;
292: }

330:                                  const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *ack,
331:                                  int result)

385: static void select_recovery_epoch(void)
386: {
387:   unsigned int i;
388:   struct recovery_epoch *epoch = NULL;
389: 
390:   for (i = 0; i < MB_RECOVERY_SLOT_COUNT; i++)
391:     {
392:       if (!g_recovery[i].probe.quarantine &&
393:           !g_recovery[i].reset_sent && !g_recovery[i].probe.busy)
394:         {
395:           epoch = &g_recovery[i];
396:           g_recovery_index = i;
397:           break;
398:         }
399:     }
400: 
401:   if (epoch == NULL)
402:     {
403:       uint32_t newest = 0;
404: 
405:       for (i = 0; i < MB_RECOVERY_SLOT_COUNT; i++)
406:         {
407:           if (g_recovery[i].probe.order >= newest)
408:             {
409:               newest = g_recovery[i].probe.order;
410:               epoch = &g_recovery[i];
411:               g_recovery_index = i;
412:             }
413:         }
414: 
415:       epoch->replay = true;
416:       g_stats.recovery_replay++;
417:     }
418:   else
419:     {
420:       memset(epoch, 0, sizeof(*epoch));
421:       epoch->reset.header = bk7258_mb_make_header(
422:         0, 0, BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX | BK7258_MB_CTRL_RESET, 0,
423:         BK7258_MB_CHAN_HW_CTRL_TX);
424:     }
425: 
426:   g_probe_attempts = 0;
427:   g_reset_pending = !epoch->replay;
428:   g_stats.recovery_cycle++;
429:   set_link_state(epoch->replay ? BK7258_MB_LINK_PROBING :
430:                                  BK7258_MB_LINK_ABORTING);
431: }

433: static void begin_abort(int result)
434: {
435:   struct active_transaction *probe = busy_probe();
436: 
437:   if (g_active.busy)
438:     {
439:       g_active.quarantine = true;
440:       complete_transaction(&g_active, NULL, result);
441:     }
442: 
443:   if (probe != NULL)
444:     {
445:       probe->quarantine = true;
446:       complete_transaction(probe, NULL, result);
447:     }
448: 
449:   fail_pending(result);
450:   g_probe_requested = false;
451:   select_recovery_epoch();
452: }

454: static struct ack_slot *alloc_ack_slot(void)
455: {
456:   unsigned int i;
457: 
458:   for (i = 0; i < MB_ACK_SLOT_COUNT; i++)
459:     {
460:       if (g_ack_slots[i].state == ACK_SLOT_FREE)
461:         {
462:           g_ack_slots[i].state = ACK_SLOT_QUEUED;
463:           return &g_ack_slots[i];
464:         }
465:     }
466: 
467:   g_stats.ack_overflow++;
468:   return NULL;
469: }

471: static int dispatch_locked(void)
472: {
473:   struct recovery_epoch *epoch = current_recovery();
474:   struct active_transaction *active;
475:   struct logical_channel *channel;
476:   unsigned int i;
477:   int ret;
478: 
479:   /* ACKs always outrank RESET and ordinary commands. */
480: 
481:   for (i = 0; i < MB_ACK_SLOT_COUNT; i++)
482:     {
483:       if (g_ack_slots[i].state != ACK_SLOT_QUEUED)
484:         {
485:           continue;
486:         }
487: 
488:       ret = send_slot(&g_ack_slots[i].message, &g_ack_slots[i].order);
489:       if (ret < 0)
490:         {
491:           return ret;
492:         }
493: 
494:       g_ack_slots[i].state = ACK_SLOT_SENT;
495:     }
496: 
497:   if (g_reset_pending)
498:     {
499:       ret = send_slot(&epoch->reset, &epoch->reset_order);
500:       if (ret < 0)
501:         {
502:           return ret;
503:         }
504: 
505:       g_reset_pending = false;
506:       epoch->reset_sent = true;
507:       set_link_state(BK7258_MB_LINK_PROBING);
508:     }
509: 
510:   if (g_active.busy || busy_probe() != NULL)
511:     {
512:       return OK;
513:     }
514: 
515:   for (i = 0; i < MB_CHANNEL_COUNT; i++)
516:     {
517:       channel = &g_channels[i];
518:       if (!channel->queued)
519:         {
520:           continue;
521:         }
522: 
523:       if (g_link_state == BK7258_MB_LINK_PROBING)
524:         {
525:           if (g_channel_ids[i] == BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX &&
526:               bk7258_mb_header_cmd(&channel->pending) ==
527:               BK7258_MB_UART_STATE)
528:             {
529:               active = &epoch->probe;
530:             }
531:           else
532:             {
533:               continue;
534:             }
535: 
536:           if (active == &epoch->probe && active->quarantine &&
537:               !epoch->replay)
538:             {
539:               return -ENOLINK;
540:             }
541:         }
542:       else if (g_link_state == BK7258_MB_LINK_READY)
543:         {
544:           active = &g_active;
545:           if (active->quarantine)
546:             {
547:               return -ENOLINK;
548:             }
549:         }
550:       else
551:         {
552:           return OK;
553:         }
554: 
555:       if (!epoch->replay || active != &epoch->probe)
556:         {
557:           memset(&active->message, 0, sizeof(active->message));
558:           memcpy(&active->message, &channel->pending,
559:                  sizeof(active->message));
560:           active->message.header = bk7258_mb_make_header(
561:             bk7258_mb_header_cmd(&channel->pending),
562:             bk7258_mb_header_state(&channel->pending), 0, ++g_tx_seq,
563:             g_channel_ids[i]);
564:         }
565: 
566:       active->callback = channel->callback;
567:       active->arg = channel->arg;
568:       active->channel_index = i;
569:       active->started = clock_systime_ticks();
570:       active->busy = true;
571:       ret = send_slot(&active->message, &active->order);
572:       if (ret < 0)
573:         {
574:           active->busy = false;
575:           return ret;
576:         }
577: 
578:       if (active == &epoch->probe)
579:         {
580:           if (epoch->first_probe_order == 0)
581:             {
582:               epoch->first_probe_order = active->order;
583:             }
584: 
585:           g_probe_attempts++;
586:           g_stats.probes++;
587:         }
588: 
589:       return OK;
590:     }
591: 
592:   return OK;
593: }

595: static uint32_t ack_header_reason(
596:   const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message,
597:   const struct active_transaction *active)
598: {
599:   uint8_t control = bk7258_mb_header_ctrl(message);
600:   uint32_t reason = 0;
601: 
602:   if (!active->busy)
603:     {
604:       return 1u;
605:     }
606: 
607:   if (control != BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX)
608:     {
609:       reason |= 2u;
610:     }
611:   if (bk7258_mb_header_channel(message) !=
612:       bk7258_mb_header_channel(&active->message))
613:     {
614:       reason |= 4u;
615:     }
616:   if (bk7258_mb_header_seq(message) !=
617:       bk7258_mb_header_seq(&active->message))
618:     {
619:       reason |= 8u;
620:     }
621:   if (bk7258_mb_header_cmd(message) !=
622:       bk7258_mb_header_cmd(&active->message))
623:     {
624:       reason |= 16u;
625:     }
626: 
627:   return reason;
628: }

630: static bool valid_uart_ack(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message)
631: {
632:   return (message->payload_address & ~3u) == 0 &&
633:          message->payload_length == 0 && message->flags == 0 &&
634:          message->crc8 == 0 && message->reserved == 0;
635: }
636: 
637: static void handle_ack(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message)
638: {
639:   struct recovery_epoch *epoch = current_recovery();
640:   struct active_transaction *active;
641:   bool replay;
642:   int result;
643:   uint32_t reason;
644: 
645: 
646:   active = busy_probe();
647:   if (active == NULL)
648:     {
649:       active = &g_active;
650:     }
651: 
652:   g_stats.last_ack_header = message->header;
653:   g_stats.last_active_header = active->message.header;
654:   reason = ack_header_reason(message, active);
655:   if (reason != 0)
656:     {
657:       g_stats.bad_ack++;
658:       g_stats.bad_ack_reason |= reason;
659:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, g_stats.last_ack_header);
660:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, g_stats.last_active_header);
661:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, g_stats.bad_ack_reason);
662:       return;
663:     }
664: 
665: 
666:   if (bk7258_mb_header_channel(message) == BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX &&
667:       !valid_uart_ack(message))
668:     {
669:       /* Keep active stable.  A malformed ACK is not an ownership proof. */
670: 
671:       g_stats.bad_ack++;
672:       g_stats.bad_ack_reason |= 32u;
673:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, g_stats.bad_ack_reason);
674:       return;
675:     }
676: 
677:   if ((bk7258_mb_header_state(message) & ~BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL) != 0)
678:     {
679:       g_stats.bad_ack++;
680:       g_stats.bad_ack_reason |= 64u;
681:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, g_stats.bad_ack_reason);
682:       return;
683:     }
684: 
685:   result = (bk7258_mb_header_state(message) & BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL) != 0 ?
686:            -EREMOTEIO : OK;
687: 
688:   if (bk7258_mb_header_channel(message) == BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX &&
689:       result == OK && (message->payload_address & 2u) != 0)
690:     {
691:       result = -EREMOTEIO;
692:     }
693: 
694:   replay = active == &epoch->probe && epoch->replay;
695:   release_acks_before(replay ? epoch->first_probe_order : active->order);
696:   if (replay)
697:     {
698:       unsigned int replay_index = g_recovery_index;
699:       unsigned int i;
700: 
701:       /* This ACK may be a late ACK for the original copy.  It proves every
702:        * older epoch was copied, but not that the new replay envelope was
703:        * copied.  Preserve the replay epoch, free only older epochs, and use
704:        * one of them for a fresh-sequence confirmation probe.
705:        */
706: 
707:       complete_transaction(active, message, -EAGAIN);
708:       g_active.quarantine = false;
709:       for (i = 0; i < MB_RECOVERY_SLOT_COUNT; i++)
710:         {
711:           if (i != replay_index)
712:             {
713:               memset(&g_recovery[i], 0, sizeof(g_recovery[i]));
714:             }
715:         }
716: 
717:       select_recovery_epoch();
718:       (void)dispatch_locked();
719:       return;
720:     }
721: 
722:   complete_transaction(active, message, result);
723: 
724:   if (active == &epoch->probe)
725:     {
726:       if (result == OK && (message->flags & 2u) == 0)
727:         {
728:           release_recovery_slots();
729:           g_recovery_index = 0;
730:           g_probe_attempts = 0;
731:           set_link_state(BK7258_MB_LINK_READY);
732:         }
733:       else if (result == -EREMOTEIO &&
734:                g_probe_attempts < MB_PROBE_MAX_ATTEMPTS)
735:         {
736:           /* CP may not have opened MB_UART0 yet.  The matched ACK proves
737:            * that this probe slot is no longer referenced by its FIFO.
738:            */
739:         }
740:       else
741:         {
742:           g_stats.probe_fail++;
743:           epoch->probe.quarantine = result == -ETIMEDOUT;
744:           set_link_state(BK7258_MB_LINK_DOWN);
745:         }
746:     }
747: 
748:   else if (bk7258_mb_header_channel(message) == BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX &&
749:            result < 0)
750:     {
751:       begin_abort(result);
752:     }
753: 
754:   (void)dispatch_locked();
755: }

757: static int handle_command(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message)
758: {
759:   struct ack_slot *slot;
760:   unsigned int rx_index;
761:   uint8_t channel = bk7258_mb_header_channel(message);
762:   uint8_t control = bk7258_mb_header_ctrl(message);
763:   uint8_t ack_flags = 0;
764:   uint8_t state = 0;
765:   int ret = -ENOSYS;
766: 
767:   g_stats.last_command_header = message->header;
768: 
769:   if ((control & BK7258_MB_CTRL_SYNC_TX) == 0)
770:     {
771:       slot = alloc_ack_slot();
772:       if (slot == NULL)
773:         {
774:           g_stats.deferred_command++;
775:           return -EAGAIN;
776:         }
777:     }
778:   else
779:     {
780:       slot = NULL;
781:     }
782: 
783:   if ((control & ~(BK7258_MB_CTRL_SYNC_TX | BK7258_MB_CTRL_RESET)) != 0 ||
784:       bk7258_mb_header_state(message) != 0 ||
785:       (channel & 0xf0u) != 0x40u)
786:     {
787:       g_stats.bad_header++;
788:       state = BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL;
789:     }
790:   else if ((rx_index = rx_channel_index(channel)) < MB_RX_CHANNEL_COUNT &&
791:            g_rx_callbacks[rx_index] != NULL)
792:     {
793:       ret = g_rx_callbacks[rx_index](message, &ack_flags,
794:                                       g_rx_args[rx_index]);
795:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
796:         {
797:           if (slot != NULL)
798:             {
799:               slot->state = ACK_SLOT_FREE;
800:             }
801: 
802:           g_stats.deferred_command++;
803:           return -EAGAIN;
804:         }
805:       else if (ret < 0)
806:         {
807:           state = BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL;
808:         }
809:     }
810:   else if (channel == BK7258_MB_CHAN_PWC_RX && g_pwc_rx != NULL)
811:     {
812:       ret = g_pwc_rx(message);
813:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
814:         {
815:           if (slot != NULL)
816:             {
817:               slot->state = ACK_SLOT_FREE;
818:             }
819: 
820:           g_stats.deferred_command++;
821:           return -EAGAIN;
822:         }
823:       else if (ret < 0)
824:         {
825:           state = BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL;
826:         }
827:     }
828:   else if (channel == BK7258_MB_CHAN_SARADC_RX &&
829:            (bk7258_mb_header_cmd(message) == 0u ||
830:             bk7258_mb_header_cmd(message) == 1u) &&
831:            message->payload_address == 1u &&
832:            message->payload_length == 0u && message->flags == 0u &&
833:            message->crc8 == 0u && message->reserved == 0u)
834:     {
835:       /* Match Armino's SARADC operation-notification ABI. */
836:       ack_flags = 2u;
837:       ret = OK;
838:     }
839:   else
840:     {
841:       g_stats.unsupported++;
842:       state = BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL;
843:     }
844: 
845:   if ((control & BK7258_MB_CTRL_SYNC_TX) != 0)
846:     {
847:       return OK;
848:     }
849: 
850:   memset(&slot->message, 0, sizeof(slot->message));
851:   slot->message.header = bk7258_mb_make_header(
852:     bk7258_mb_header_cmd(message), state, BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX,
853:     bk7258_mb_header_seq(message), channel);
854:   slot->message.payload_address = ack_flags;
855: 
856:   if (ack_slots_used() >= MB_ACK_HIGH_WATER)
857:     {
858:       g_probe_requested = true;
859:     }
860: 
861:   (void)dispatch_locked();
862:   return OK;
863: }

865: static int mailbox_rx(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message)
866: {
867:   irqstate_t flags;
868:   uint8_t control;
869: 
870:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
871:   g_stats.rx++;
872:   control = bk7258_mb_header_ctrl(message);
873: 
874:   if ((control & BK7258_MB_CTRL_RESET) != 0)
875:     {
876:       if ((control & BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX) == 0 ||
877:           (bk7258_mb_header_channel(message) & 0xf0u) != 0x40u ||
878:           (control & ~(BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX | BK7258_MB_CTRL_RESET)) != 0)
879:         {
880:           g_stats.bad_header++;
881:         }
882:       else
883:         {
884:           g_stats.resets++;
885:           g_peer_reset_generation++;
886:           bk7258_mbox_discard_deferred();
887:           begin_abort(-ECONNRESET);
888:         }
889:     }
890:   else if ((control & BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX) != 0)
891:     {
892:       handle_ack(message);
893:     }
894:   else
895:     {
896:       int ret = handle_command(message);
897: 
898:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
899:         {
900:           rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
901:           return ret;
902:         }
903:     }
904: 
905:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
906:   nxsem_post(&g_tx_sem);
907:   return OK;
908: }

910: static int mailbox_diag_worker(int argc, char **argv)
911: {
912:   enum bk7258_mb_link_state reported = BK7258_MB_LINK_QUIESCING;
913:   int ret;
914: 
915:   (void)argc;
916:   (void)argv;
917:   ret = bind_worker_to_primary();
918:   if (ret < 0)
919:     {
920:       return -EXDEV;
921:     }
922: 
923:   for (;;)
924:     {
925:       nxsem_wait_uninterruptible(&g_diag_sem);
926:       nxsem_reset(&g_diag_sem, 0);
927:       irqstate_t flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
928:       enum bk7258_mb_link_state state = g_diag_state;
929:       bk7258_mb_link_callback_t callback = g_link_callback;
930:       void *callback_arg = g_link_arg;
931:       uint32_t timeout = g_stats.timeout;
932:       uint32_t bad_ack = g_stats.bad_ack;
933:       uint8_t epoch = g_recovery_index;
934: 
935:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
936:       if (reported == state)
937:         {
938:           continue;
939:         }
940: 
941:       reported = state;
942:       if (reported != BK7258_MB_LINK_PROBING &&
943:           reported != BK7258_MB_LINK_READY)
944:         {
945:           syslog(LOG_WARNING,
946:                  "mailbox: link state=%u epoch=%u timeout=%lu bad_ack=%lu\n",
947:                  reported, epoch, (unsigned long)timeout,
948:                  (unsigned long)bad_ack);
949:         }
950: 
951:       if (callback != NULL)
952:         {
953:           callback(reported, callback_arg);
954:         }
955:     }
956: 
957:   return OK;
958: }

960: static int mailbox_tx_worker(int argc, char **argv)
961: {
962:   int ret;
963: 
964:   (void)argc;
965:   (void)argv;
966:   ret = bind_worker_to_primary();
967:   if (ret < 0)
968:     {
969:       ret = -EXDEV;
970:     }
971: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
972:   else if (!bk7258_smp_secondary_is_ready())
973:     {
974:       ret = -EAGAIN;
975:     }
976: #endif
977:   if (ret < 0)
978:     {
979:       return ret;
980:     }
981: 
982:   for (;;)
983:     {
984:       struct active_transaction *probe;
985:       irqstate_t flags;
986:       bool request_probe;
987: 
988:       (void)nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible(&g_tx_sem, MB_WORK_INTERVAL);
989:       nxsem_reset(&g_tx_sem, 0);
990:       flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
991: 
992:       probe = busy_probe();
993:       if ((g_active.busy &&
994:            clock_systime_ticks() - g_active.started >= MB_TIMEOUT) ||
995:           (probe != NULL &&
996:            clock_systime_ticks() - probe->started >= MB_TIMEOUT))
997:         {
998:           g_stats.timeout++;
999:           bk7258_boottrace_detail(3,
1000:             (g_stats.last_tx_error & 0xffu) |
1001:             ((g_stats.timeout & 0xffu) << 8) |
1002:             ((g_stats.fifo_full & 0xffu) << 16) |
1003:             ((g_stats.ack_overflow & 0xffu) << 24));
1004:           if (probe != NULL)
1005:             {
1006:               probe->quarantine = true;
1007:               complete_transaction(probe, NULL, -ETIMEDOUT);
1008:               g_stats.probe_fail++;
1009:               set_link_state(BK7258_MB_LINK_DOWN);
1010:             }
1011:           else
1012:             {
1013:               begin_abort(-ETIMEDOUT);
1014:             }
1015:         }
1016: 
1017:       if (g_link_state == BK7258_MB_LINK_DOWN &&
1018:           clock_systime_ticks() - g_down_since >= MB_DOWN_RETRY)
1019:         {
1020:           select_recovery_epoch();
1021:         }
1022: 
1023:       (void)dispatch_locked();
1024:       if (g_probe_requested && ack_slots_used() < MB_ACK_HIGH_WATER)
1025:         {
1026:           g_probe_requested = false;
1027:         }
1028: 
1029:       request_probe = g_probe_requested &&
1030:                       g_link_state == BK7258_MB_LINK_READY &&
1031:                       !g_channels[4].queued && !g_active.busy;
1032:       if (request_probe)
1033:         {
1034:           g_probe_requested = false;
1035:         }
1036: 
1037:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1038: 
1039:       if (request_probe)
1040:         {
1041:           bk7258_mb_uart_request_state();
1042:         }
1043:     }
1044: 
1045:   return OK;
1046: }

1076: int bk7258_mailbox_workers_start(void)
1077: {
1078:   cpu_set_t cpuset;
1079:   int ret;
1080: 
1081:   if (!g_initialized)
1082:     {
1083:       return -EAGAIN;
1084:     }
1085: 
1086:   if (g_workers_started)
1087:     {
1088:       return OK;
1089:     }
1090: 
1091:   ret = wait_secondary_scheduler();
1092:   if (ret < 0)
1093:     {
1094:       return ret;
1095:     }
1096: 
1097: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
1098:   /* All physical CP descriptors must originate on logical CPU0.  Pin the
1099:    * creator before activating the workers so their inherited affinity is
1100:    * CPU0-only from their first scheduled instruction. */
1101: 
1102:   CPU_ZERO(&cpuset);
1103:   CPU_SET(0, &cpuset);
1104:   ret = sched_setaffinity(0, sizeof(cpuset), &cpuset);
1105:   if (ret < 0)
1106:     {
1107:       return ret;
1108:     }
1109: #endif
1110: 
1111:   if (!g_tx_worker_created)
1112:     {
1113:       /* Discard wakeups accumulated before a worker existed.  Transport
1114:        * state remains authoritative and will be checked on the first timed
1115:        * worker pass. */
1116: 
1117:       nxsem_reset(&g_tx_sem, 0);
1118:       ret = kthread_create("mbox-v2", MB_TX_PRIORITY, 2048,
1119:                            mailbox_tx_worker, NULL);
1120:       if (ret < 0)
1121:         {
1122:           return ret;
1123:         }
1124: 
1125:       g_tx_worker_created = true;
1126:       g_tx_worker_pid = ret;
1127:     }
1128: 
1129:   if (!g_diag_worker_created)
1130:     {
1131:       nxsem_reset(&g_diag_sem, 0);
1132:       ret = kthread_create("mbox-diag", 80, 1024, mailbox_diag_worker, NULL);
1133:       if (ret < 0)
1134:         {
1135:           return ret;
1136:         }
1137: 
1138:       g_diag_worker_created = true;
1139:     }
1140: 
1141:   g_workers_started = true;
1142:   return OK;
1143: }

1145: int bk7258_mailbox_workers_activate(void)
1146: {
1147:   struct sched_param param;
1148: 
1149:   if (!g_workers_started || g_tx_worker_pid < 0)
1150:     {
1151:       return -EAGAIN;
1152:     }
1153: 
1154:   param.sched_priority = MB_TX_PRIORITY;
1155:   return sched_setparam(g_tx_worker_pid, &param) < 0 ? -errno : OK;

1182: int bk7258_mailbox_send_wire(uint8_t logical_channel,
1183:                              const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message,
1184:                              bk7258_mb_tx_complete_t callback, void *arg)
1185: {
1186:   struct logical_channel *channel;
1187:   unsigned int index;
1188:   irqstate_t flags;
1189: 
1190:   if (!g_initialized || !g_physical_started || message == NULL)
1191:     {
1192:       return -EAGAIN;
1193:     }
1194: 
1195:   index = channel_index(logical_channel);
1196:   if (index >= MB_CHANNEL_COUNT)
1197:     {
1198:       return -EINVAL;
1199:     }
1200: 
1201:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
1202:   channel = &g_channels[index];
1203: 
1204:   if (channel->queued)
1205:     {
1206:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1207:       return -EBUSY;
1208:     }
1209: 
1210:   if (g_link_state != BK7258_MB_LINK_READY &&
1211:       !(g_link_state == BK7258_MB_LINK_PROBING &&
1212:         logical_channel == BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX &&
1213:         bk7258_mb_header_cmd(message) == BK7258_MB_UART_STATE))
1214:     {
1215:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1216:       return -ENOLINK;
1217:     }
1218: 
1219:   if (g_link_state == BK7258_MB_LINK_READY && g_active.quarantine)
1220:     {
1221:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1222:       return -ENOLINK;
1223:     }
1224: 
1225:   memset(&channel->pending, 0, sizeof(channel->pending));
1226:   memcpy(&channel->pending, message, sizeof(channel->pending));
1227:   channel->callback = callback;
1228:   channel->arg = arg;
1229:   channel->result = -EINPROGRESS;
1230:   channel->queued = true;
1231: 
1232:   if (up_cpu_index() == 0)
1233:     {
1234:       (void)dispatch_locked();
1235:     }
1236: 
1237:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1238: 
1239:   /* CPU1 callers only enqueue work.  Physical descriptors to the CP still
1240:    * originate exclusively from logical CPU0.
1241:    */
1242: 
1243:   nxsem_post(&g_tx_sem);
1244:   return OK;
1245: }

1262: int bk7258_mailbox_start_probe(void)
1263: {

1265: 
1266:   if (!g_initialized)

1269:     }
1270: 
1271:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);

1273:     {

1277:    * wait loop and the UART worker can request a probe concurrently; reopening
1278:    * a READY link here would abort a valid state ACK and race the first PWC
1279:    * transaction. */

1326: int bk7258_mailbox_wait_link_ready(unsigned int timeout_ms)
1327: {
1328:   clock_t deadline = clock_systime_ticks() + MSEC2TICK(timeout_ms);
1329:   clock_t next_probe = clock_systime_ticks();
1330: 
1331:   while (!bk7258_mailbox_link_ready())
1332:     {
1333:       clock_t now = clock_systime_ticks();
1334: 
1335:       if ((int32_t)(clock_systime_ticks() - deadline) >= 0)
1336:         {
1337:           return -ETIMEDOUT;
1338:         }
1339: 
1340:       /* Keep the boot-time probe self-starting even if the initial
1341:        * ABORTING -> PROBING worker wakeup was consumed before RESET was
1342:        * dispatched.  This only marks STATE pending; normal transaction
1343:        * serialization remains in the mailbox workers. */
1344:       if ((int32_t)(now - next_probe) >= 0)
1345:         {
1346:           /* The TX worker can complete STATE between the loop condition and
1347:            * this retry point.  Do not reopen a link that has just become
1348:            * ready. */
1349:           if (!bk7258_mailbox_link_ready())
1350:             {
1351:               bk7258_mailbox_start_probe();
1352:               bk7258_mb_uart_request_state();
1353:             }
1354:           next_probe = now + MSEC2TICK(100);
1355:         }
1356: 
1357:       bk7258_mbox_kick_rx();
1358:       nxsig_usleep(1000);
1359:     }
1360: 
1361:   return OK;
1362: }

1411: static int wait_channel(uint8_t logical_channel, unsigned int timeout_ms)
1412: {
1413:   unsigned int index = channel_index(logical_channel);
1414:   clock_t deadline = clock_systime_ticks() + MSEC2TICK(timeout_ms);
1415: 
1416:   if (index >= MB_CHANNEL_COUNT)
1417:     {
1418:       return -EINVAL;
1419:     }
1420: 
1421:   for (;;)
1422:     {
1423:       irqstate_t flags;
1424:       bool queued;
1425:       int result;
1426: 
1427:       flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
1428:       queued = g_channels[index].queued;
1429:       result = g_channels[index].result;
1430:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1431:       if (!queued)
1432:         {
1433:           return result == -EINPROGRESS ? OK : result;
1434:         }
1435: 
1436:       if ((int32_t)(clock_systime_ticks() - deadline) >= 0)
1437:         {
1438:           bk7258_mailbox_dump_stats();
1439:           return -ETIMEDOUT;
1440:         }
1441: 
1442:       /* UART link bring-up drains the physical mailbox explicitly because
1443:        * the IRQ may not be dispatched while board_late_initialize() owns the
1444:        * boot transaction.  PWC waits run in the same context and need the
1445:        * same progress guarantee; otherwise CP can process 0x5 and enqueue its
1446:        * ACK while AP remains asleep waiting for an IRQ-side drain. */
1447:       bk7258_mbox_kick_rx();
1448:       nxsig_usleep(1000);
1449:     }
1450: }

1453: {

1455: }

1457: int bk7258_mailbox_wait_pwc(unsigned int timeout_ms)
1458: {
1459:   return wait_channel(BK7258_MB_CHAN_PWC_TX, timeout_ms);
1460: }

241: static int bk7258_mbox_irq(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
242: {
243:   uintptr_t rdata0;
244:   uintptr_t rdata1;
245:   uintptr_t sidreg;
246:   int cpu = up_cpu_index();
247:   unsigned int budget = MBOX_IRQ_DRAIN_BUDGET;
248: 
249:   (void)irq;
250:   (void)context;
251:   (void)arg;
252: 
253:   mbox_clear_errors(cpu);
254:   if (cpu == 1 && bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() >=
255:                   BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ACK &&
256:                   bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() <
257:                   BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_ENTER)
258:     {
259:       bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_ENTER);
260:     }
261:   sidreg = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_SID : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_SID;
262:   rdata0 = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_RDATA0 : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_RDATA0;
263:   rdata1 = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_RDATA1 : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_RDATA1;
264: 
265:   while ((bk7258_mbox_rx_status() & 2u) == 0 && budget-- != 0)
266:     {
267:       struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc;
268:       uint32_t address;
269:       uint32_t length;
270:       uint8_t source;
271: 
272:       if (cpu == 0)
273:         {
274:           mbox_process_desc();
275:         }
276: 
277:       desc = cpu == 0 ? mbox_alloc_desc() : NULL;
278:       if (cpu == 0 && desc == NULL)
279:         {
280:           g_stats.descriptor_full++;
281:           mbox_trace_errors();
282:           break;
283:         }
284: 
285:       source = getreg32(sidreg) & 0x0fu;
286:       address = getreg32(rdata0);
287:       length = getreg32(rdata1);
288: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
289:       if (length == 0)
290:         {
291:           if (source == (uint8_t)(2 - cpu))
292:             {
293:               if (cpu == 1 && address == BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK)
294:                 {
295:                   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_RAW);
296:                 }
297: 
298:               bk7258_smp_ipi_receive(irq, context, address);
299:             }
300:           else
301:             {
302:               if (cpu == 0)
303:                 {
304:                   g_stats.bad_source++;
305:                   mbox_trace_errors();
306:                 }
307:             }
308: 
309:           continue;
310:         }
311: #endif
312: 
313:       if (cpu != 0)
314:         {
315:           continue;
316:         }
317: 
318:       if (!mbox_valid_envelope(source, address, length))
319:         {
320:           continue;
321:         }
322: 
323:       __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
324:       memcpy(&desc->message, (const void *)(uintptr_t)address,
325:              sizeof(desc->message));
326:       desc->order = ++g_rx_order;
327:       desc->used = true;
328:       g_stats.rx_messages++;
329:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, desc->message.header);
330:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, address);
331:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, g_stats.rx_messages);
332:       mbox_process_desc();
333:     }
334: 
335:   if (cpu == 0)
336:     {
337:       mbox_process_desc();
338:     }
339: 
340:   if (cpu == 1 && bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() ==
341:                   BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_RAW)
342:     {
343:       bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_EXIT);
344:     }
345: 
346:   return OK;
347: }

159:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, bk7258_mbox_smp_ready());

206:       if (bk7258_smp_boot_notified() && !ping_sent)
207:         {
208:           if (bk7258_smp_boot_ping(1) < 0)

211:             }

179:  *   SMP function call handler
180:  *
181:  * Input Parameters:
182:  *   irq     - Interrupt id
183:  *   context - Regs context before irq
184:  *   arg     - Interrupt arg
185:  *
186:  * Returned Value:
187:  *   Result
188:  *
189:  ****************************************************************************/
190: 
191: int nxsched_smp_call_handler(int irq, FAR void *context,
192:                              FAR void *arg)
193: {
194:   FAR sq_queue_t *call_queue;
195:   FAR sq_entry_t *curr;
196:   FAR sq_entry_t *next;
197:   int cpu = this_cpu();
198: 
199:   irqstate_t flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_smp_call_lock);
200: 
201:   call_queue = &g_smp_call_queue[cpu];
202: 
203:   sq_for_every_safe(call_queue, curr, next)
204:     {
205:       FAR struct smp_call_data_s *data =
206:         container_of(curr, struct smp_call_data_s, node[cpu]);
207:       FAR struct smp_call_cookie_s *cookie;
208:       int ret;
209: 
210:       sq_rem(&data->node[cpu], call_queue);
211: 
212:       spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_smp_call_lock, flags);
213: 
214:       ret = data->func(data->arg);
215: 
216:       flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_smp_call_lock);
217: 
218:       cookie = data->cookie;
219:       if (cookie != NULL)
220:         {
221:           if (ret < 0)
222:             {
223:               cookie->error = ret;
224:             }
225: 
226:           /* Insert ack back to original cpu call queue,
227:            * add direct avoid nxsched_smp_call_add g_smp_call_lock again.
228:            */
229: 
230: #if CONFIG_SMP_CALL_POOL_COUNT > 0
231:           sq_addlast(&cookie->ack.node[cookie->cpu],
232:                      &g_smp_call_queue[cookie->cpu]);
233:           up_send_smp_call(1 << cookie->cpu);
234: #else
235:           nxsem_post(&cookie->sem);
236: #endif
237:         }
238:     }
239: 
240:   spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_smp_call_lock, flags);
241:   return OK;
242: }

312: int nxsched_smp_call(cpu_set_t cpuset, nxsched_smp_call_t func,
313:                      FAR void *arg)
314: {
315:   FAR struct smp_call_cookie_s *c;
316:   int semcount;
317:   int cpucnt;
318:   int ret = OK;
319:   int i;
320: 
321: #if CONFIG_SMP_CALL_POOL_COUNT > 0
322:   c = nxsched_smp_call_cookie_alloc();
323: #else
324:   struct smp_call_cookie_s cookie;
325: 
326:   c = &cookie;
327: #endif
328: 
329:   nxsched_smp_call_cookie_init(c, func, arg);
330: 
331:   ret = nxsched_smp_call_async(cpuset, &c->req);
332: 
333:   if (ret < 0)
334:     {
335:       nxsem_destroy(&c->sem);
336:       return ret;
337:     }
338: 
339:   cpucnt = CPU_COUNT(&cpuset);
340:   if (up_interrupt_context())
341:     {
342:       /* Wait until completion. */
343: 
344:       do
345:         {
346:           nxsem_get_value(&c->sem, &semcount);
347:         }
348:       while (semcount != cpucnt);
349:     }
350:   else
351:     {
352:       for (i = 0; i < cpucnt; i++)
353:         {
354:           int rc = nxsem_wait_uninterruptible(&c->sem);
355:           if (rc < 0)
356:             {
357:               ret = rc;
358:             }
359:         }
360:     }
361: 
362:   if (c->error < 0)
363:     {
364:       ret = c->error;
365:     }
366: 
367:   nxsched_smp_call_cookie_free(c);
368:   return ret;
369: }

461:             }
462:         }
463: 
464:       CPU_CLR(this_cpu(), &cpuset);
465:     }

481:             }
482:         }

486:

488:   if (!up_interrupt_context())

43: static inline_function
44: int get_blocking(FAR sem_t *sem, bool mutex, bool *blocking)
45: {
46:   int32_t mholder = NXSEM_NO_MHOLDER;
47:   int ret = OK;
48: 
49:   if (mutex)
50:     {
51:       /* Mutex post from interrupt context is not allowed */
52: 
53:       DEBUGASSERT(!up_interrupt_context());
54: 
55:       /* Lock the mutex for us by setting the blocking bit */
56: 
57:       mholder = atomic_or(NXSEM_MHOLDER(sem), NXSEM_MBLOCKING_BIT);
58: 
59:       /* Mutex post from another thread is not allowed, unless
60:        * called from nxsem_reset
61:        */
62: 
63:       DEBUGASSERT(mholder == (NXSEM_MBLOCKING_BIT | NXSEM_NO_MHOLDER) ||
64:                   (mholder & (~NXSEM_MBLOCKING_BIT)) == nxsched_gettid());
65: 
66:       *blocking = NXSEM_MBLOCKING(mholder);
67: 
68:       if (!(*blocking))
69:         {
70:           atomic_set(NXSEM_MHOLDER(sem), NXSEM_NO_MHOLDER);
71:         }
72:     }
73:   else
74:     {
75:       int32_t sem_count;
76: 
77:       /* Check the maximum allowable value */
78: 
79:       sem_count = atomic_read(NXSEM_COUNT(sem));
80:       do
81:         {
82:           if (sem_count >= SEM_VALUE_MAX)
83:             {
84:               ret = -EOVERFLOW;
85:               break;
86:             }
87:         }
88:       while (!atomic_try_cmpxchg_release(NXSEM_COUNT(sem), &sem_count,
89:                                          sem_count + 1));
90:       *blocking = sem_count < 0;
91:     }
92: 
93:   return ret;
94: }

102:  *
103:  * Description:
104:  *   When a kernel thread has finished with a semaphore, it will call
105:  *   nxsem_post().  This function unlocks the semaphore referenced by sem
106:  *   by performing the semaphore unlock operation on that semaphore.
107:  *
108:  *   If the semaphore value resulting from this operation is positive, then
109:  *   no tasks were blocked waiting for the semaphore to become unlocked; the
110:  *   semaphore is simply incremented.
111:  *
112:  *   If the value of the semaphore resulting from this operation is zero,
113:  *   then one of the tasks blocked waiting for the semaphore shall be
114:  *   allowed to return successfully from its call to nxsem_wait().
115:  *
116:  * Input Parameters:
117:  *   sem - Semaphore descriptor
118:  *
119:  * Returned Value:
120:  *   This is an internal OS interface and should not be used by applications.
121:  *   It follows the NuttX internal error return policy:  Zero (OK) is
122:  *   returned on success.  A negated errno value is returned on failure.
123:  *
124:  * Assumptions:
125:  *   This function may be called from an interrupt handler.
126:  *
127:  ****************************************************************************/
128: 
129: int nxsem_post_slow(FAR sem_t *sem)
130: {
131:   FAR struct tcb_s *stcb = NULL;
132:   irqstate_t flags;
133: #if defined(CONFIG_PRIORITY_INHERITANCE) || defined(CONFIG_PRIORITY_PROTECT)
134:   uint8_t proto;
135: #endif
136:   bool blocking = false;
137:   bool mutex = NXSEM_IS_MUTEX(sem);
138:   int ret = OK;
139: 
140:   /* The following operations must be performed with interrupts
141:    * disabled because sem_post() may be called from an interrupt
142:    * handler.
143:    */
144: 
145:   flags = enter_critical_section();
146: 
147:   ret = get_blocking(sem, mutex, &blocking);
148: 
149:   if (ret == OK)
150:     {
151:       /* Perform the semaphore unlock operation, releasing this task as a
152:        * holder then also incrementing the count on the semaphore.
153:        *
154:        * NOTE:  When semaphores are used for signaling purposes, the holder
155:        * of the semaphore may not be this thread!  In this case,
156:        * nxsem_release_holder() will do nothing.
157:        *
158:        * In the case of a mutex this could be simply resolved since there is
159:        * only one holder but for the case of counting semaphores, there may
160:        * be many holders and if the holder is not this thread, then it is
161:        * not possible to know which thread/holder should be released.
162:        *
163:        * For this reason, it is recommended that priority inheritance be
164:        * disabled via nxsem_set_protocol(SEM_PRIO_NONE) when the semaphore is
165:        * initialized if the semaphore is to used for signaling purposes.
166:        */
167: 
168:       if (!mutex || blocking)
169:         {
170:           nxsem_release_holder(sem);
171:         }
172: 
173: #if defined(CONFIG_PRIORITY_INHERITANCE) || defined(CONFIG_PRIORITY_PROTECT)
174:       /* Don't let any unblocked tasks run until we complete any priority
175:        * restoration steps.  Interrupts are disabled, but we do not want
176:        * the head of the ready-to-run list to be modified yet.
177:        *
178:        * NOTE: If this sched_lock is called from an interrupt handler, it
179:        * will do nothing.
180:        */
181: 
182:       proto = sem->flags & SEM_PRIO_MASK;
183:       if (proto != SEM_PRIO_NONE)
184:         {
185:           sched_lock();
186:         }
187: #endif
188: 
189:       /* If the result of semaphore unlock is non-positive, then
190:        * there must be some task waiting for the semaphore.
191:        */
192: 
193:       if (blocking)
194:         {
195:           /* Check if there are any tasks in the waiting for semaphore
196:            * task list that are waiting for this semaphore.  This is a
197:            * prioritized list so the first one we encounter is the one
198:            * that we want.
199:            */
200: 
201:           stcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_remfirst(SEM_WAITLIST(sem));
202:           if (stcb != NULL)
203:             {
204:               FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
205: 
206:               /* The task will be the new holder of the semaphore when
207:                * it is awakened.
208:                */
209: 
210:               if (mutex)
211:                 {
212:                   int32_t blocking_bit = dq_empty(SEM_WAITLIST(sem)) ?
213:                     0 : NXSEM_MBLOCKING_BIT;
214:                   atomic_set(NXSEM_MHOLDER(sem), stcb->pid | blocking_bit);
215:                 }
216:               else
217:                 {
218:                   nxsem_add_holder_tcb(stcb, sem);
219:                 }
220: 
221:               /* Stop the watchdog timer */
222: 
223:               wd_cancel(&stcb->waitdog);
224: 
225:               /* Indicate that the wait is over. */
226:

44: /****************************************************************************
45:  * Name: nxsem_wait_slow
46:  *
47:  * Description:
48:  *   This function attempts to lock the semaphore referenced by 'sem' in
49:  *   slow mode.
50:  *
51:  *   This is an internal OS interface.  It is functionally equivalent to
52:  *   sem_wait except that:
53:  *
54:  *   - It is not a cancellation point, and
55:  *   - It does not modify the errno value.
56:  *
57:  * Input Parameters:
58:  *   sem - Semaphore descriptor.
59:  *
60:  * Returned Value:
61:  *   This is an internal OS interface and should not be used by applications.
62:  *   It follows the NuttX internal error return policy:  Zero (OK) is
63:  *   returned on success.  A negated errno value is returned on failure.
64:  *   Possible returned errors:
65:  *
66:  *   - EINVAL:  Invalid attempt to get the semaphore
67:  *   - EINTR:   The wait was interrupted by the receipt of a signal.
68:  *
69:  ****************************************************************************/
70: 
71: int nxsem_wait_slow(FAR sem_t *sem)
72: {
73:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
74:   irqstate_t flags;
75:   int ret = OK;
76:   bool unlocked;
77:   int32_t mholder;
78:   FAR struct tcb_s *htcb = NULL;
79:   bool mutex = NXSEM_IS_MUTEX(sem);
80: 
81:   /* The following operations must be performed with interrupts
82:    * disabled because nxsem_post() may be called from an interrupt
83:    * handler.
84:    */
85: 
86:   flags = enter_critical_section();
87: 
88:   /* Make sure we were supplied with a valid semaphore. */
89: 
90:   /* Check if the lock is available */
91: 
92:   if (mutex)
93:     {
94:       /* We lock the mutex for us by setting the blocks bit,
95:        * this is all that is needed if we block
96:        */
97: 
98:       mholder = atomic_or(NXSEM_MHOLDER(sem), NXSEM_MBLOCKING_BIT);
99: 
100:       /* Avoid mutex recursion, which is not allowed. */
101: 
102:       DEBUGASSERT((mholder & (~NXSEM_MBLOCKING_BIT)) != nxsched_gettid());
103: 
104:       if (NXSEM_MACQUIRED(mholder))
105:         {
106:           /* htcb gets NULL if
107:            * - the only holder did exit (without posting first)
108:            * - the mutex was reset before
109:            * In both cases we simply acquire the mutex, thus recovering
110:            * from these situations.
111:            */
112: 
113:           htcb = nxsched_get_tcb(mholder & (~NXSEM_MBLOCKING_BIT));
114:         }
115: 
116:       unlocked = htcb == NULL;
117:       if (!unlocked)
118:         {
119:           nxsem_add_holder_tcb(htcb, sem);
120:           nxsched_put_tcb(htcb);
121:         }
122:     }
123:   else
124:     {
125:       unlocked = atomic_sub(NXSEM_COUNT(sem), 1) > 0;
126:     }
127: 
128:   if (unlocked)
129:     {
130:       /* It is, let the task take the semaphore. */
131: 
132: #ifdef CONFIG_PRIORITY_PROTECT
133:       ret = nxsem_protect_wait(sem);
134:       if (ret < 0)
135:         {
136:           if (mutex)
137:             {
138:               atomic_set(NXSEM_MHOLDER(sem), NXSEM_NO_MHOLDER);
139:             }
140:           else
141:             {
142:               atomic_add(NXSEM_COUNT(sem), 1);
143:             }
144: 
145:           leave_critical_section(flags);
146:           return ret;
147:         }
148: #endif
149: 
150:       /* For mutexes, we only add the holder to the tasks list at the
151:        * time when a task blocks on the mutex, for priority restoration
152:        */
153: 
154:       if (mutex)
155:         {
156:           mholder = rtcb->pid;
157: 
158:           if (!dq_empty(SEM_WAITLIST(sem)))
159:             {
160:               mholder |= NXSEM_MBLOCKING_BIT;

40: /****************************************************************************
41:  * Name:  nxsched_add_readytorun
42:  *
43:  * Description:
44:  *   This function adds a TCB to the ready to run list.  If the currently
45:  *   active task has preemption disabled and the new TCB would cause this
46:  *   task to be pre-empted, the new task is added to the g_pendingtasks list
47:  *   instead.  The pending tasks will be made ready-to-run when preemption is
48:  *   unlocked.
49:  *
50:  * Input Parameters:
51:  *   btcb - Points to the blocked TCB that is ready-to-run
52:  *
53:  * Returned Value:
54:  *   true if the currently active task (the head of the ready-to-run list)
55:  *   has changed.
56:  *
57:  * Assumptions:
58:  * - The caller has established a critical section before calling this
59:  *   function (calling sched_lock() first is NOT a good idea -- use
60:  *   enter_critical_section()).
61:  * - The caller has already removed the input rtcb from whatever list it
62:  *   was in.
63:  * - The caller handles the condition that occurs if the head of the
64:  *   ready-to-run list is changed.
65:  *
66:  ****************************************************************************/
67: 
68: #ifndef CONFIG_SMP
69: bool nxsched_add_readytorun(FAR struct tcb_s *btcb)
70: {
71:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
72:   bool ret;
73: 
74:   /* Check if pre-emption is disabled for the current running task and if
75:    * the new ready-to-run task would cause the current running task to be
76:    * pre-empted.  NOTE that IRQs disabled implies that pre-emption is
77:    * also disabled.
78:    */
79: 
80:   if (rtcb->lockcount > 0 && rtcb->sched_priority < btcb->sched_priority)
81:     {
82:       /* Yes.  Preemption would occur!  Add the new ready-to-run task to the
83:        * g_pendingtasks task list for now.
84:        */
85: 
86:       nxsched_add_prioritized(btcb, list_pendingtasks());
87:       btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_PENDING;
88:       ret = false;
89:     }
90: 
91:   /* Otherwise, add the new task to the ready-to-run task list */
92: 
93:   else if (nxsched_add_prioritized(btcb, list_readytorun()))
94:     {
95:       /* The new btcb was added at the head of the ready-to-run list.  It
96:        * is now the new active task!
97:        */
98: 
99:       DEBUGASSERT(rtcb->lockcount == 0 && !is_idle_task(btcb));
100: 
101:       btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_RUNNING;
102:       btcb->flink->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN;
103:       up_update_task(btcb);
104:       ret = true;
105:     }
106:   else
107:     {
108:       /* The new btcb was added in the middle of the ready-to-run list */
109: 
110:       btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN;
111:       ret = false;
112:     }
113: 
114:   return ret;
115: }
116: 
117: #else /* !CONFIG_SMP */
118: 
119: /****************************************************************************
120:  * Name:  nxsched_switch_running
121:  *
122:  * Description:
123:  *   This function switches the head of the current CPU's assigned tasks
124:  *   list to the TCB given as parameter. The idle task is not switched out.
125:  *   If the running task can't be swapped out, the btcb is pushed to
126:  *   the ready-to-run list.
127:  *
128:  * Input Parameters:
129:  *   cpu          - Always this_cpu(). Given as argument only for
130:  *                  optimization
131:  *   switch_equal - When true, switch away a task of equal priority compared
132:  *                  to the pending one
133:  *
134:  * Returned Value:
135:  *   true if the currently active task is switched
136:  *
137:  * Assumptions:
138:  * - The caller has established a critical section
139:  * - The caller has already removed the input rtcb from whatever list it
140:  *   was in.
141:  * - The caller handles the condition that occurs if the head of the
142:  *   assigned tasks list has changed.
143:  *
144:  ****************************************************************************/
145: 
146: bool nxsched_switch_running(int cpu, bool switch_equal)
147: {
148:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = current_task(cpu);
149:   int sched_priority = rtcb->sched_priority;
150:   FAR struct tcb_s *btcb;
151:   bool ret = false;
152: 
153:   DEBUGASSERT(cpu == this_cpu());
154: 
155:   if (nxsched_islocked_tcb(rtcb))
156:     {
157:       return false;
158:     }
159: 
160:   if (switch_equal && sched_priority > 0)
161:     {
162:       sched_priority--;
163:     }
164: 
165:   /* If there is a task in readytorun list, which is eglible to run on this
166:    * CPU, and has higher priority than the current task,
167:    * switch the current task to that one.
168:    */
169: 
170:   for (btcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_readytorun());
171:        btcb && btcb->sched_priority > sched_priority;
172:        btcb = btcb->flink)
173:     {
174:       /* Check if the task found in ready-to-run list is allowed to run on
175:        * this CPU. TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED may be used to override affinity. If
176:        * the flag is set, assume that btcb->cpu is valid, and it is the only
177:        * CPU on which the btcb can run.
178:        */
179: 
180:       if (CPU_ISSET(cpu, &btcb->affinity) &&
181:           ((btcb->flags & TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED) == 0 || btcb->cpu == cpu))
182:         {
183:           /* Found a task, remove it from ready-to-run list */
184: 
185:           dq_rem((FAR struct dq_entry_s *)btcb, list_readytorun());
186: 
187:           if (!is_idle_task(rtcb))
188:             {
189:               /* Put currently running task back to ready-to-run list */
190: 
191:               rtcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN;
192:               nxsched_add_prioritized(rtcb, list_readytorun());
193:             }
194:           else
195:             {
196:               rtcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_ASSIGNED;
197:             }
198: 
199:           per_cpu_var_smp(g_assignedtasks, cpu) = btcb;
200:           up_update_task(btcb);
201: 
202:           btcb->cpu = cpu;
203:           btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_RUNNING;
204:           ret = true;
205:           break;
206:         }
207:     }
208: 
209:   return ret;
210: }

212: /****************************************************************************
213:  * Name:  nxsched_add_readytorun
214:  *
215:  * Description:
216:  *   This function adds a TCB to one of the ready to run lists. The list
217:  *   will be:
218:  *
219:  *   1. The g_readytorun list if the task is ready-to-run but not running
220:  *      and not assigned to a CPU.
221:  *   2. The g_assignedtask[cpu] list if the task is running or if has been
222:  *      assigned to a CPU.
223:  *
224:  *   If the currently active task has preemption disabled and the new TCB
225:  *   would cause this task to be pre-empted, the new task is added to the
226:  *   g_pendingtasks list instead.  The pending tasks will be made
227:  *   ready-to-run when preemption isunlocked.
228:  *
229:  * Input Parameters:
230:  *   btcb - Points to the blocked TCB that is ready-to-run
231:  *
232:  * Returned Value:
233:  *   true if the currently active task (the head of the ready-to-run list)
234:  *   has changed.
235:  *
236:  * Assumptions:
237:  * - The caller has established a critical section before calling this
238:  *   function (calling sched_lock() first is NOT a good idea -- use
239:  *   enter_critical_section()).
240:  * - The caller has already removed the input rtcb from whatever list it
241:  *   was in.
242:  * - The caller handles the condition that occurs if the head of the
243:  *   ready-to-run list has changed.
244:  *
245:  ****************************************************************************/
246: 
247: bool nxsched_add_readytorun(FAR struct tcb_s *btcb)
248: {
249:   bool doswitch = false;
250:   int target_cpu = btcb->flags & TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED ? btcb->cpu :
251:     nxsched_select_cpu(btcb->affinity);
252:   FAR struct tcb_s *tcb = current_task(target_cpu);
253: 
254:   /* Add the btcb to the ready to run list, and try to run it on the target
255:    * CPU
256:    */
257: 
258:   btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN;
259:   nxsched_add_prioritized(btcb, list_readytorun());
260: 
261:   /* In some cases, such as setaffinity, cpu need to be used. */
262: 
263:   btcb->cpu = target_cpu;
264:   if (tcb->sched_priority < btcb->sched_priority)
265:     {
266:       doswitch = nxsched_deliver_task(this_cpu(), target_cpu,
267:                                       SWITCH_HIGHER);
268:     }
269: 
270:   return doswitch;
271: }

42: /****************************************************************************
43:  * Name: nxsched_set_affinity
44:  *
45:  * Description:
46:  *   sched_setaffinity() sets the CPU affinity mask of the thread whose ID
47:  *   is pid to the value specified by mask.  If pid is zero, then the
48:  *   calling thread is used.  The argument cpusetsize is the length (i
49:  *   bytes) of the data pointed to by mask.  Normally this argument would
50:  *   be specified as sizeof(cpu_set_t).
51:  *
52:  *   If the thread specified by pid is not currently running on one of the
53:  *   CPUs specified in mask, then that thread is migrated to one of the
54:  *   CPUs specified in mask.
55:  *
56:  *   nxsched_set_affinity() is identical to the function sched_setparam(),
57:  *   differing only in its return value:  This function does not modify
58:  *   the errno variable.  This is a non-standard, internal OS function and
59:  *   is not intended for use by application logic.  Applications should
60:  *   use the standard sched_setparam().
61:  *
62:  * Input Parameters:
63:  *   pid        - The ID of thread whose affinity set will be modified.
64:  *   cpusetsize - Size of mask.  MUST be sizeofcpu_set_t().
65:  *   mask       - The location to return the thread's new affinity set.
66:  *
67:  * Returned Value:
68:  *   Zero (OK) if successful.  Otherwise, a negated errno value is returned:
69:  *
70:  *     ESRCH  The task whose ID is pid could not be found.
71:  *
72:  ****************************************************************************/
73:

116:     }

118:   /* Set the new affinity mask. */

122:   /* Is the task still executing a a CPU in its affinity mask? Will this

127:    */

130:       tcb->task_state <= LAST_READY_TO_RUN_STATE)
131:     {

133:        * affinity mask?

140:            *

145:            */

17: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_REENTER     0xa2000000u
18: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_OWNER_BUSY  0xa3000000u
19: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_INTENT      0xa4000000u
20: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_CONFLICT    0xa5000000u
21: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ACQUIRED    0xa6000000u
22: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_UNLOCK      0xa7000000u
23: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_RELEASED    0xa8000000u
24: 
25: struct bk7258_atomic_gate_s
26: {
27:   volatile uint32_t interested[2];
28:   volatile uint32_t turn;
29:   volatile uint32_t owner;
30:   volatile uint32_t depth;
31: };
32: 
33: static struct bk7258_atomic_gate_s g_bk7258_atomic_gate
34:   __attribute__((section(".bk_spinlock"), aligned(32)));
35: 
36: static inline void bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(unsigned int cpu, uint32_t value)
37: {
38:   if (cpu == 0 && (bk7258_boottrace_words()[6] & 0xffu) == 2u)
39:     {
40:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(4, value);
41:     }
42: }
43: 
44: static bool bk7258_hwspinlock_trylock(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
45: {
46:   unsigned int cpu = (unsigned int)up_cpu_index();
47:   unsigned int other = cpu ^ 1u;
48: 
49:   (void)dev;
50:   DEBUGASSERT(cpu < 2);
51:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ENTRY);
52: 
53:   /* BK7258 has only two SRAM exclusive monitors while CP, AP CPU1 and AP
54:    * CPU2 are all active.  Keep the AP-only atomic gate independent of
55:    * LDAEX/STREX so CP traffic cannot starve an AP exclusive sequence.
56:    */
57: 
58:   /* libc atomics are normally short, but the scheduler's recursive critical
59:    * section can issue another atomic operation on the same CPU.  Re-entry
60:    * must be decided before entering Peterson arbitration; otherwise a waiter
61:    * on the other CPU can make the current owner wait for itself.
62:    */
63: 
64:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner == cpu + 1u)
65:     {
66:       if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth == UINT32_MAX)
67:         {
68:           PANIC();
69:         }
70: 
71:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth++;
72:       UP_DMB();
73:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_REENTER |
74:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth);
75:       return true;
76:     }
77: 
78:   /* This is only a fast rejection.  The Peterson protocol below remains
79:    * authoritative while a new owner is between intent and owner publish.
80:    */
81: 
82:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner != 0)
83:     {
84:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_OWNER_BUSY |
85:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner);
86:       return false;
87:     }
88: 
89:   /* Every attempt must publish a fresh intent and turn.  Leaving intent set
90:    * after a failed trylock makes the state stale and breaks trylock's
91:    * one-attempt contract.
92:    */
93: 
94:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 1;
95:   UP_DMB();
96:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn = other;
97:   UP_DMB();
98:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_INTENT);
99: 
100:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[other] != 0 &&
101:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn == other)
102:     {
103:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 0;
104:       UP_DMB();
105:       __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
106:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_CONFLICT);
107:       return false;
108:     }
109: 
110:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = cpu + 1u;
111:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth = 1;
112:   UP_DMB();
113:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ACQUIRED);
114:   return true;
115: }
116: 
117: static void bk7258_hwspinlock_relax(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
118: {
119:   (void)dev;
120:   __asm__ volatile("nop" ::: "memory");
121: }
122: 
123: static void bk7258_hwspinlock_unlock(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
124: {
125:   unsigned int cpu = (unsigned int)up_cpu_index();
126: 
127:   (void)dev;
128:   if (cpu >= 2 || g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner != cpu + 1u ||
129:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth == 0)
130:     {
131:       PANIC();
132:     }
133: 
134:   if (--g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth != 0)
135:     {
136:       UP_DMB();
137:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_UNLOCK |
138:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth);
139:       return;
140:     }
141: 
142:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = 0;
143:   UP_DMB();
144:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 0;
145:   UP_DSB();
146:   __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
147:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_RELEASED);
148: }

150: const struct hwspinlock_ops_s g_bk7258_hwspinlock_ops =
151: {
152:   .trylock = bk7258_hwspinlock_trylock,
153:   .relax   = bk7258_hwspinlock_relax,
154:   .unlock  = bk7258_hwspinlock_unlock
155: };

160:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[1] = 0;
161:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn = 0;
162:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = 0;
163:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth = 0;
164:   UP_DSB();

82:   int ret;
83: 
84:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&g_psram_power_lock);

86:     {
87:       return ret;
88:     }
89: 
90:   ret = nxsem_reset(&g_psram_power_sem, 0);

92:     {
93:       nxmutex_unlock(&g_psram_power_lock);

95:     }
96: 
97:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
98:   g_psram_power_expected_state = state;
99:   g_psram_power_state = UINT32_MAX;
100:   g_psram_power_result = -EINPROGRESS;
101:   g_psram_power_version = 0;
102:   g_psram_power_waiting = true;
103:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);

105:   ret = pwc_send_wait(PM_CTRL_PSRAM_POWER_CMD,
106:                       PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_CPU1, state,
107:                       PM_PSRAM_PROTO_V1);

109:     {
110:       transport_ret = OK;
111:       response_ret = nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible(
112:                        &g_psram_power_sem,
113:                        MSEC2TICK(PM_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS));
114:       ret = transport_ret != OK ? transport_ret : response_ret;
115:       if (ret > 0)
116:         {
117:           ret = -EIO;
118:         }
119:     }
120:   else if (ret > 0)
121:     {
122:       ret = -EIO;
123:     }
124: 
125:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
126:   g_psram_power_waiting = false;
127:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
128: 
129:   if (ret == OK && (g_psram_power_state != state ||
130:                     g_psram_power_result != OK ||
131:                     g_psram_power_version != PM_PSRAM_PROTO_V1))

133:       ret = g_psram_power_result < 0 ? g_psram_power_result : -EPROTO;
134:     }

136:   if (ret < 0)
137:     {
138:       printf("PWC: PSRAM power %s failed, error=%d result=%ld "
139:              "state=%lu version=%lu\n",

141:              (long)g_psram_power_result,
142:              (unsigned long)g_psram_power_state,
143:              (unsigned long)g_psram_power_version);

163:   if (ret == OK)
164:     {
165:       ret = bk7258_mailbox_wait_pwc(PM_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS);
166:       if (ret > 0)
167:         {

174:     }

180: static int openvela_ready_request(uint32_t ready, int32_t cause,
181:                                   int32_t *semantic_result)
182: {
183:   irqstate_t flags;
184:   bool received;
185:   uint32_t echo;
186:   uint32_t version;
187:   int32_t result;
188:   int ret;
189: 
190:   ret = nxsem_reset(&g_openvela_ready_sem, 0);
191:   if (ret < 0)
192:     {
193:       return ret;
194:     }
195: 
196:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
197:   g_openvela_ready_expected = ready;
198:   g_openvela_ready_echo = UINT32_MAX;
199:   g_openvela_ready_result = -EINPROGRESS;
200:   g_openvela_ready_version = 0;
201:   g_openvela_ready_received = false;
202:   g_openvela_ready_waiting = true;
203:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
204: 
205:   ret = pwc_send_wait(PM_OPENVELA_READY_CMD, ready, (uint32_t)cause,
206:                       PM_OPENVELA_READY_PROTO_V1);
207:   if (ret == OK)
208:     {
209:       ret = nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible(&g_openvela_ready_sem,
210:                                            MSEC2TICK(PM_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS));
211:     }
212: 
213:   if (ret > 0)
214:     {
215:       ret = -EIO;
216:     }
217: 
218:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
219:   g_openvela_ready_waiting = false;
220:   received = g_openvela_ready_received;
221:   echo = g_openvela_ready_echo;
222:   result = g_openvela_ready_result;
223:   version = g_openvela_ready_version;
224:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
225: 
226:   if (ret == OK && (!received || echo != ready ||
227:                     version != PM_OPENVELA_READY_PROTO_V1))
228:     {
229:       ret = -EPROTO;
230:     }
231: 
232:   if (ret == OK)
233:     {
234:       *semantic_result = result;
235:     }
236: 
237:   return ret;
238: }

240: static int openvela_ready_abort(int error)
241: {
242:   int ret;
243: 
244:   if (error >= 0)
245:     {
246:       error = -EIO;
247:     }

250:    * reset/power off this core while handling the request, so an application
251:    * response cannot be required on the abort path.

290: static int pwc_rx(const void *raw)
291: {
292:   const uint8_t *bytes = raw;
293:   struct pwc_message message;
294:   unsigned int next;
295: 
296:   if (bytes == NULL)
297:     {
298:       return -EINVAL;
299:     }
300: 
301:   /* The logical mailbox invokes PWC callbacks while holding the driver lock.
302:    * Keep the queue update in that critical section instead of recursively
303:    * acquiring the non-recursive SMP spinlock here. */
304: 
305:   next = (g_head + 1u) % PM_QUEUE_DEPTH;
306:   if (next == g_tail)
307:     {
308:       return -EAGAIN;
309:     }
310: 
311:   message.header = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[0];
312:   message.param1 = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[1];
313:   message.param2 = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[2];
314:   message.param3 = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[3];
315:   g_queue[g_head] = message;
316:   g_head = next;
317:   nxsem_post(&g_pwc_sem);
318:   return OK;
319: }
320: 
321: static int pwc_worker(int argc, char **argv)
322: {
323:   int ret = OK;
324: 
325:   (void)argc;
326:   (void)argv;
327:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_PWC_WORKER_ENTER);
328: 
329:   /* bk7258_mailbox_workers_start() pinned the bring-up thread to CPU0.
330:    * Kernel threads inherit that affinity before activation, so changing the
331:    * running PWC worker's affinity here is redundant and can trigger another
332:    * SMP scheduler transaction during the boot handshake. */
333: 
334:   g_worker_result = OK;
335:   g_worker_ready = true;
336:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_PWC_WORKER_READY);
337:   nxsem_post(&g_worker_sem);
338: 
339:   for (;;)
340:     {
341:       struct pwc_message message;
342:       irqstate_t flags;
343: 
344:       nxsem_wait_uninterruptible(&g_pwc_sem);
345:       flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
346:       message = g_queue[g_tail];
347:       g_tail = (g_tail + 1u) % PM_QUEUE_DEPTH;
348:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
349:       /* A full software queue leaves the physical descriptor deferred with
350:        * no transport ACK.  Freeing one entry is the progress event that must
351:        * retry that descriptor even when no new mailbox IRQ arrives. */
352: 
353:       bk7258_mbox_kick_rx();
354:       /* Hardware power/clock actions stay in this thread, never in IRQ. */
355:       switch (message.header & 0xffu)
356:         {
357:           case PM_CTRL_PSRAM_POWER_CMD:
358:             flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
359:             if (g_psram_power_waiting &&
360:                 message.param1 == g_psram_power_expected_state)
361:               {
362:                 g_psram_power_state = message.param1;
363:                 g_psram_power_result = (int32_t)message.param2;
364:                 g_psram_power_version = message.param3;
365:                 g_psram_power_waiting = false;
366:                 nxsem_post(&g_psram_power_sem);
367:               }
368:             rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
369:             break;
370: 
371:           case PM_OPENVELA_READY_CMD:
372:             flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
373:             if (g_openvela_ready_waiting &&
374:                 message.param1 == g_openvela_ready_expected)
375:               {
376:                 g_openvela_ready_echo = message.param1;
377:                 g_openvela_ready_result = (int32_t)message.param2;
378:                 g_openvela_ready_version = message.param3;
379:                 g_openvela_ready_received = true;
380:                 g_openvela_ready_waiting = false;
381:                 nxsem_post(&g_openvela_ready_sem);
382:               }
383:             rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
384:             break;
385: 
386: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_PSRAM
387:           case PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD:
388:             if (message.param1 == 0u)
389:               {
390:                 ret = pwc_send_wait(PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD,
391:                                     PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD,
392:                                     bk7258_psram_heap_used(), 0);
393:                 if (ret != OK)
394:                   {
395:                     printf("PWC: PSRAM malloc state response failed, "
396:                            "error=%d\n", ret);
397:                   }
398:               }
399:             else if (message.param1 == PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF)
400:               {
401:                 /* This CP notification is sent after physical power-down. */
402: 
403:                 bk7258_psram_power_lost();
404:               }
405:             break;
406: 
407:           case PM_CP1_DUMP_PSRAM_MALLOC_INFO_CMD:
408:             bk7258_psram_dump();
409:             break;
410: 
411:           case PM_CP1_RECOVERY_CMD:
412:             {
413: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
414:               ret = pwc_send_wait(PM_CP1_RECOVERY_CMD,
415:                                   PM_RECOVERY_STATE_INIT,
416:                                   (uint32_t)-ENOTSUP, 0);
417: #else
418:               int shutdown_ret = bk7258_psram_shutdown();
419: 
420:               ret = pwc_send_wait(
421:                       PM_CP1_RECOVERY_CMD, PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_CPU1,
422:                       shutdown_ret == 0 ? PM_RECOVERY_STATE_FINISH :
423:                                           PM_RECOVERY_STATE_INIT, 0);
424: #endif
425:               if (ret != OK)
426:                 {
427:                   printf("PWC: recovery response failed, error=%d\n", ret);
428:                 }
429:             }
430:             break;
431: #endif
432: 
433:           default:
434:             break;
435:         }
436:     }
437:   return 0;
438: }

440: int bk7258_pwc_start(void)
441: {
442:   int pid;
443:   int ret;
444:
