1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * BK7258 Armino-compatible HW_CTRL power-up and heartbeat service.
3:  ****************************************************************************/
4: 
5: #include <nuttx/config.h>
6: 
7: #include <errno.h>
8: #include <stdbool.h>
9: #include <stdint.h>
10: #include <stdio.h>
11: #include <string.h>
12: #include <syslog.h>
13: 
14: #include <nuttx/clock.h>
15: #include <nuttx/kthread.h>
16: #include <nuttx/mutex.h>
17: #include <nuttx/sched.h>
18: #include <nuttx/signal.h>
19: 
20: #include "hardware/bk7258_mbox.h"
21: #define IPC_CPU1_POWER_UP_INDICATION   1u
22: #define IPC_CPU1_HEART_BEAT_INDICATION 2u
23: #define IPC_ACK_STATE_COMPLETE         2u
24: #define IPC_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS        600u
25: #define IPC_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL         MSEC2TICK(2000)
26: #define IPC_HEARTBEAT_RETRY            MSEC2TICK(100)
27: #define IPC_HEARTBEAT_POLL_US           10000u
28: #define IPC_HEARTBEAT_PRIORITY          110
29: 
30: static mutex_t g_ipc_lock = NXMUTEX_INITIALIZER;
31: static volatile int g_ipc_ack_result;
32: static volatile int g_ipc_start_result;
33: static volatile int g_heartbeat_result;
34: static volatile bool g_heartbeat_enabled;
35: static volatile bool g_heartbeat_pending;
36: static volatile uint32_t g_heartbeat_completions;
37: static clock_t g_next_heartbeat;
38: static uint32_t g_heartbeat_failures;
39: static uint32_t g_heartbeat_submissions;
40: static uint32_t g_heartbeat_reported;
41: static bool g_ipc_started;
42: 
43: static int bind_worker_to_primary(void)
44: {
45: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
46:   cpu_set_t cpuset;
47: 
48:   CPU_ZERO(&cpuset);
49:   CPU_SET(0, &cpuset);
50:   return sched_setaffinity(0, sizeof(cpuset), &cpuset);
51: #else
52:   return OK;
53: #endif
54: }
55: 
56: static int ipc_ack_result(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *ack,
57:                           int result)
58: {
59:   if (result == OK &&
60:       (ack == NULL || ack->reserved != IPC_ACK_STATE_COMPLETE))
61:     {
62:       result = -EREMOTEIO;
63:     }
64: 
65:   return result;
66: }
67: 
68: static void ipc_tx_complete(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *ack,
69:                               int result, void *arg)
70: {
71:   g_ipc_ack_result = ipc_ack_result(ack, result);
72:   if ((uintptr_t)arg == IPC_CPU1_POWER_UP_INDICATION &&
73:       g_ipc_ack_result == OK)
74:     {
75:       g_heartbeat_result = OK;
76:       g_next_heartbeat = clock_systime_ticks() + IPC_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL;
77:       g_heartbeat_enabled = true;
78:     }
79: }
80: 
81: static void ipc_heartbeat_complete(
82:   const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *ack, int result, void *arg)
83: {
84:   (void)arg;
85:   g_heartbeat_result = ipc_ack_result(ack, result);
86:   g_heartbeat_completions++;
87:   g_heartbeat_pending = false;
88: }
89: 
90: static int ipc_send(uint8_t command, uint32_t parameter)
91: {
92:   struct bk7258_mb_wire_message message;
93:   volatile uint32_t *payload =
94:     (volatile uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)BK7258_IPC_TX_ADDRESS;
95:   int ret;
96: 
97:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&g_ipc_lock);
98:   if (ret < 0)
99:     {
100:       return ret;
101:     }
102: 
103:   *payload = parameter;
104:   __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
105: 
106:   memset(&message, 0, sizeof(message));
107:   message.header = command;
108:   message.payload_address = BK7258_IPC_TX_ADDRESS;
109:   message.payload_length =
110:     command == IPC_CPU1_HEART_BEAT_INDICATION ? sizeof(*payload) : 0;
111:   g_ipc_ack_result = -EINPROGRESS;
112: 
113:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_send_wire(BK7258_MB_CHAN_HW_CTRL_TX, &message,
114:                                   ipc_tx_complete,
115:                                   (void *)(uintptr_t)command);
116:   if (ret == OK)
117:     {
118:       ret = bk7258_mailbox_wait_hw_control(IPC_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS);
119:       if (ret == OK)
120:         {
121:           ret = g_ipc_ack_result;
122:         }
123:     }
124: 
125:   nxmutex_unlock(&g_ipc_lock);
126:   return ret > 0 ? -EIO : ret;
127: }
128: 
129: static int ipc_heartbeat_worker(int argc, char **argv)
130: {
131:   int ret;
132: 
133:   (void)argc;
134:   (void)argv;
135: 
136:   ret = bind_worker_to_primary();
137:   if (ret < 0)
138:     {
139:       return -EXDEV;
140:     }
141: 
142:   for (;;)
143:     {
144:       nxsig_usleep(IPC_HEARTBEAT_POLL_US);
145:       bk7258_ipc_heartbeat_poll();
146:     }
147: 
148:   return OK;
149: }
150: 
151: void bk7258_ipc_heartbeat_poll(void)
152: {
153:   struct bk7258_mb_wire_message message;
154:   volatile uint32_t *payload =
155:     (volatile uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)BK7258_IPC_TX_ADDRESS;
156:   clock_t now;
157:   int ret;
158: 
159:   if (!g_heartbeat_enabled || g_heartbeat_pending)
160:     {
161:       return;
162:     }
163: 
164:   if (g_heartbeat_completions != g_heartbeat_reported)
165:     {
166:       g_heartbeat_reported = g_heartbeat_completions;
167:       if (g_heartbeat_reported <= 3u)
168:         {
169:           printf("IPC: heartbeat ACK result=%d count=%lu\n",
170:                  g_heartbeat_result,
171:                  (unsigned long)g_heartbeat_reported);
172:         }
173:     }
174: 
175:   if (g_heartbeat_result < 0)
176:     {
177:       g_heartbeat_failures++;
178:       if ((g_heartbeat_failures & (g_heartbeat_failures - 1u)) == 0)
179:         {
180:           syslog(LOG_ERR, "IPC heartbeat failed: %d count=%lu\n",
181:                  g_heartbeat_result,
182:                  (unsigned long)g_heartbeat_failures);
183:         }
184: 
185:       g_heartbeat_result = OK;
186:     }
187: 
188:   now = clock_systime_ticks();
189:   if ((sclock_t)(now - g_next_heartbeat) < 0)
190:     {
191:       return;
192:     }
193: 
194:   *payload = 0;
195:   __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
196:   memset(&message, 0, sizeof(message));
197:   message.header = IPC_CPU1_HEART_BEAT_INDICATION;
198:   message.payload_address = BK7258_IPC_TX_ADDRESS;
199:   message.payload_length = sizeof(*payload);
200:   g_heartbeat_result = -EINPROGRESS;
201:   g_heartbeat_pending = true;
202:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_send_wire(BK7258_MB_CHAN_HW_CTRL_TX, &message,
203:                                  ipc_heartbeat_complete, NULL);
204:   if (ret == OK)
205:     {
206:       g_heartbeat_submissions++;
207:       g_next_heartbeat = now + IPC_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL;
208:       if (g_heartbeat_submissions <= 3u)
209:         {
210:           printf("IPC: heartbeat queued count=%lu tick=%llu\n",
211:                  (unsigned long)g_heartbeat_submissions,
212:                  (unsigned long long)now);
213:         }
214:     }
215:   else
216:     {
217:       g_heartbeat_pending = false;
218:       g_heartbeat_result = ret;
219:       g_next_heartbeat = now + IPC_HEARTBEAT_RETRY;
220:     }
221: }
222: 
223: int bk7258_ipc_heartbeat_start(void)
224: {
225:   int pid;
226:   int ret;
227: 
228:   if (g_ipc_started)
229:     {
230:       return g_ipc_start_result;
231:     }
232: 
233:   g_ipc_start_result = -EINPROGRESS;
234:   g_heartbeat_enabled = false;
235:   g_heartbeat_pending = false;
236:   g_heartbeat_completions = 0;
237:   g_heartbeat_failures = 0;
238:   g_heartbeat_submissions = 0;
239:   g_heartbeat_reported = 0;
240:   ret = bind_worker_to_primary();
241:   if (ret < 0)
242:     {
243:       g_ipc_start_result = -EXDEV;
244:     }
245:   else
246:     {
247:       ret = ipc_send(IPC_CPU1_POWER_UP_INDICATION, 0);
248:       g_ipc_start_result = ret < 0 ? ret : OK;
249:     }
250: 
251:   if (g_ipc_start_result == OK)
252:     {
253:       pid = kthread_create("ipc-heartbeat", IPC_HEARTBEAT_PRIORITY, 1536,
254:                            ipc_heartbeat_worker, NULL);
255:       if (pid < 0)
256:         {
257:           g_ipc_start_result = pid;
258:         }
259:     }
260: 
261:   g_ipc_started = g_ipc_start_result == OK;
262: 
263:   if (g_ipc_start_result == OK)
264:     {
265:       printf("IPC: HW_CTRL power-up acknowledged by CP, heartbeat armed "
266:              "now=%llu deadline=%llu\n",
267:              (unsigned long long)clock_systime_ticks(),
268:              (unsigned long long)g_next_heartbeat);
269:     }
270: 
271:   return g_ipc_start_result;
272: }

100: /****************************************************************************
101:  * Name:  nxsched_process_roundrobin
102:  *
103:  * Description:
104:  *   Check if the currently executing task has exceeded its time slice.
105:  *
106:  * Input Parameters:
107:  *   tcb - The TCB of the currently executing task
108:  *   ticks - The number of ticks that have elapsed on the interval timer.
109:  *   noswitches - True: Can't do context switches now.
110:  *
111:  * Returned Value:
112:  *   The number if ticks remaining until the next time slice expires.
113:  *   CLOCK_MAX is returned if there is no time slicing (i.e., the task at
114:  *   the head of the ready-to-run list does not support round robin
115:  *   scheduling).
116:  *
117:  *   The value one may returned under certain circumstances that probably
118:  *   can't happen.  The value one is the minimal timer setup and it means
119:  *   that a context switch is needed now, but cannot be performed because
120:  *   noswitches == true.
121:  *
122:  * Assumptions:
123:  *   - Interrupts are disabled
124:  *   - The task associated with TCB uses the round robin scheduling
125:  *     policy
126:  *
127:  ****************************************************************************/
128: 
129: clock_t nxsched_process_roundrobin(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb, clock_t ticks,
130:                                    bool noswitches)
131: {
132:   FAR struct tcb_s *ptcb;  /* Pointer to the next ready-to-run TCB */
133:   clock_t ret;
134:   int decr;
135: 
136:   /* How much can we decrement the timeslice delay?  If 'ticks' is greater
137:    * than the timeslice value, then we ignore any excess amount.
138:    *
139:    * 'ticks' should not be greater than the remaining timeslice.  But that
140:    * event seems to be possible, perhaps in cases where pre-emption has been
141:    * disabled or the noswitches flag is set.  This might cause jitter of a
142:    * few ticks in the slicing because the excess amount is not handled.
143:    */
144: 
145:   DEBUGASSERT(tcb != NULL);
146:   decr = MIN(tcb->timeslice, ticks);
147: 
148:   /* Decrement the timeslice counter */
149: 
150:   tcb->timeslice -= decr;
151: 
152:   /* Did decrementing the timeslice counter cause the timeslice to expire? */
153: 
154:   ret = tcb->timeslice;
155:   if (tcb->timeslice <= 0 && !nxsched_islocked_tcb(tcb))
156:     {
157:       /* We will also suppress context switches if we were called via one
158:        * of the unusual cases handled by nxsched_reassess_timer().  In that
159:        * case, we will return a value of one so that the timer will expire
160:        * as soon as possible and we can perform this action in the normal
161:        * timer expiration context.
162:        *
163:        * This is kind of kludge, but I am not to concerned because I hope
164:        * that the situation is impossible or at least could only occur on
165:        * rare corner-cases.
166:        */
167: 
168:       if (noswitches)
169:         {
170:           ret = 0;
171:         }
172:       else
173:         {
174:           /* Reset the timeslice. */
175: 
176:           tcb->timeslice = MSEC2TICK(CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL);
177:           ret = tcb->timeslice;
178: 
179:           /* We know we are at the head of the ready to run prioritized
180:            * list.  We must be the highest priority task eligible for
181:            * execution.  Check the next task in the ready to run list.  If
182:            * it is the same priority, then we need to relinquish the CPU and
183:            * give that task a shot.
184:            */
185: 
186: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
187:           ptcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_readytorun());
188: #else
189:           ptcb = tcb->flink;
190: #endif
191:           if (ptcb &&
192:               ptcb->sched_priority >= tcb->sched_priority)
193:             {
194:               FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
195: 
196:               /* Just resetting the task priority to its current value.
197:                * This will cause the task to be rescheduled behind any
198:                * other tasks at the same priority.
199:                */
200: 
201: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
202:               DEBUGASSERT(tcb->task_state == TSTATE_TASK_RUNNING);
203:               if (tcb->cpu != this_cpu())
204:                 {
205:                   nxsched_smp_call_init(&g_call_data,
206:                                         nxsched_roundrobin_handler,
207:                                         (FAR void *)(uintptr_t)tcb->pid);
208:                   nxsched_smp_call_single_async(tcb->cpu, &g_call_data);
209:                 }
210:               else if (nxsched_switch_running(tcb->cpu, true))
211: #else
212:               if (nxsched_reprioritize_rtr(tcb, tcb->sched_priority))
213: #endif
214:                 {
215:                   nxsched_switch(this_task(), rtcb);
216:                 }
217:             }
218:         }
219:     }
220:   else if (tcb->timeslice == 0)
221:     {
222:       ret = CLOCK_MAX;
223:     }
224: 
225:   return ret;
226: }

307: /* Get/set the PRIMASK register */
308: 
309: static inline_function uint8_t getprimask(void)
310: {
311:   uint32_t primask;
312:   __asm__ __volatile__
313:     (
314:      "\tmrs  %0, primask\n"
315:      : "=r" (primask)
316:      :
317:      : "memory");

320: }

323: {
324:   __asm__ __volatile__

326:       "\tmsr primask, %0\n"
327:       :
328:       : "r" (primask)
329:       : "memory");
330: }

332: /* Get/set the BASEPRI register.  The BASEPRI register defines the minimum
333:  * priority for exception processing. When BASEPRI is set to a nonzero
334:  * value, it prevents the activation of all exceptions with the same or
335:  * lower priority level as the BASEPRI value.
336:  */
337: 
338: static inline_function uint8_t getbasepri(void)
339: {
340:   uint32_t basepri;
341: 
342:   __asm__ __volatile__
343:     (
344:      "\tmrs  %0, basepri\n"
345:      : "=r" (basepri)
346:      :
347:      : "memory");
348: 
349:   return (uint8_t)basepri;
350: }
351: 
352: static inline_function void setbasepri(uint32_t basepri)
353: {
354:   __asm__ __volatile__
355:     (
356:       "\tmsr basepri, %0\n"
357:       :
358:       : "r" (basepri)
359:       : "memory");
360: }
361: 
362: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV7M_BASEPRI_WAR  /* Cortex-M7 r0p1 Errata 837070 Workaround */
363: /* Set the BASEPRI register (possibly increasing the priority).
364:  *
365:  * This may be retaining or raising priority.  Cortex-M7 r0p1 Errata
366:  * 837070 Workaround may be required if we are raising the priority.
367:  */
368: 
369: static always_inline_function void raisebasepri(uint32_t basepri)
370: {
371:   register uint32_t primask;
372: 
373:   /* 1. Retain the previous value of the PRIMASK register,
374:    * 2  Disable all interrupts via the PRIMASK register.  NOTE:  They
375:    *    could possibly already be disabled.
376:    * 3. Set the BASEPRI register as requested (possibly increasing the
377:    *    priority)
378:    * 4. Restore the original value of the PRIMASK register, probably re-
379:    *    enabling interrupts.  This avoids the possibly undesirable side-
380:    *    effect of unconditionally re-enabling interrupts.
381:    */
382: 
383: #pragma GCC diagnostic push /* primask is initialized in ASM */
384: #pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Wuninitialized"
385: #pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Wmaybe-uninitialized"
386:   __asm__ __volatile__
387:     (
388:      "\tmrs   %0, primask\n"
389:      "\tcpsid i\n"
390:      "\tmsr   basepri, %1\n"
391:      "\tmsr   primask, %0\n"
392:      : "+r" (primask)
393:      : "r"  (basepri)
394:      : "memory");
395: #pragma GCC diagnostic pop
396: }
397: #else
398: #  define raisebasepri(b) setbasepri(b);
399: #endif

403: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_ARMV6M
404: static inline_function void up_irq_disable(void)
405: {
406:   __asm__ __volatile__ ("\tcpsid  i\n");
407: }

413: {
414:   unsigned short primask;
415: 
416:   /* Return the current value of primask register and set
417:    * bit 0 of the primask register to disable interrupts
418:    */
419: 
420:   __asm__ __volatile__
421:     (
422:      "\tmrs    %0, primask\n"
423:      "\tcpsid  i\n"
424:      : "=r" (primask)
425:      :
426:      : "memory");
427: 
428:   return primask;
429: }

432: 
433: static inline_function void up_irq_enable(void)
434: {
435:   __asm__ __volatile__ ("\tcpsie  i\n");
436: }

445:    */

449:       "\tmsr primask, %0\n"

451:       : "r" (flags)

48: /****************************************************************************
49:  * Name: nxthread_create
50:  *
51:  * Description:
52:  *   This function creates and activates a new thread of the specified type
53:  *   with a specified priority and returns its system-assigned ID.  It is the
54:  *   internal, common implementation of task_create() and kthread_create().
55:  *   See comments with task_create() for further information.
56:  *
57:  * Input Parameters:
58:  *   name       - Name of the new task
59:  *   ttype      - Type of the new task
60:  *   priority   - Priority of the new task
61:  *   stack_addr - Address of the stack needed
62:  *   stack_size - Size (in bytes) of the stack needed
63:  *   entry      - Entry point of a new task
64:  *   arg        - A pointer to an array of input parameters.  The array
65:  *                should be terminated with a NULL argv[] value. If no
66:  *                parameters are required, argv may be NULL.
67:  *   envp       - A pointer to an array of environment strings. Terminated
68:  *                with a NULL entry.
69:  *
70:  * Returned Value:
71:  *   Returns the positive, non-zero process ID of the new task or a negated
72:  *   errno value to indicate the nature of any failure.  If memory is
73:  *   insufficient or the task cannot be created -ENOMEM will be returned.
74:  *
75:  ****************************************************************************/
76: 
77: int nxthread_create(FAR const char *name, int ttype, int priority,
78:                     FAR void *stack_addr, int stack_size, main_t entry,
79:                     FAR char * const argv[], FAR char * const envp[])
80: {
81:   posix_spawnattr_t attr;
82:   FAR struct tcb_s *tcb;
83:   pid_t pid;
84:   int ret = -ENOMEM;
85: 
86:   posix_spawnattr_init(&attr);
87:   posix_spawnattr_setstacksize(&attr, (size_t)stack_size);
88:   posix_spawnattr_setstackaddr(&attr, stack_addr);
89:   posix_spawnattr_setpriority(&attr, priority);
90: 
91:   /* Allocate a TCB for the new task. */
92: 
93:   tcb = kmm_zalloc(ttype == TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_KERNEL ?
94:                    sizeof(struct tcb_s) :
95:                    sizeof(struct tcb_s) + sizeof(struct task_group_s));
96:   if (!tcb)
97:     {
98:       serr("ERROR: Failed to allocate TCB\n");
99:     }
100:   else
101:     {
102:       /* Setup the task type */
103: 
104:       atomic_set(&tcb->flags, ttype | TCB_FLAG_FREE_TCB);
105: 
106:       /* Initialize the task */
107: 
108:       ret = nxtask_init(tcb, name, entry, NULL, &attr, argv, envp);
109:       posix_spawnattr_destroy(&attr);
110:       if (ret < OK)
111:         {
112:           kmm_free(tcb);
113:         }
114:       else
115:         {
116:           /* Get the assigned pid before we start the task */
117: 
118:           pid = tcb->pid;
119: 
120:           /* Activate the task */
121: 
122:           nxtask_activate(tcb);
123: 
124:           ret = pid;
125:         }
126:     }
127: 
128:   return ret;
129: }

47:  * Description:
48:  *   This function sets the priority of a running task.  This does nothing
49:  *   if we are increasing the priority of a running task.  If we are dropping
50:  *   the priority of a running task, then this could cause then next lower
51:  *   priority task to run,
52:  *
53:  *   NOTE: Setting a task's priority to the same value has a similar effect
54:  *   to sched_yield() -- The task will be moved to after all other tasks
55:  *   with the same priority.
56:  *
57:  * Input Parameters:
58:  *   tcb - the TCB of task to reprioritize.
59:  *   sched_priority - The new task priority
60:  *
61:  * Returned Value:
62:  *   None
63:  *
64:  ****************************************************************************/
65: 
66: static inline void nxsched_running_setpriority(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb,
67:                                                int sched_priority)
68: {
69:   FAR struct tcb_s *nxttcb;
70: 
71:   /* Get the TCB of the next highest priority, ready to run task */
72: 
73: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
74:   nxttcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_readytorun());
75: #else
76:   nxttcb = tcb->flink;
77: #endif
78: 
79:   /* A context switch will occur if the new priority of the running
80:    * task becomes less than OR EQUAL TO the next highest priority
81:    * ready to run task.
82:    */
83: 
84: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
85: 
86:   /* A context switch will occur:
87:    * CASE 1. The new priority of the running task becomes less than or
88:    * equal to the next highest priority ready to run task.
89:    * CASE 2. In SMP, the affinity of tcb has changed and no longer includes
90:    * the current cpu.
91:    */
92: 
93:   if ((nxttcb && sched_priority <= nxttcb->sched_priority) ||
94:       (tcb->affinity & (1 << tcb->cpu)) == 0)
95: #else
96:   if (nxttcb && sched_priority <= nxttcb->sched_priority)
97: #endif
98:     {
99: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
100:       tcb->sched_priority = sched_priority;
101:       if (nxsched_deliver_task(this_cpu(), tcb->cpu, SWITCH_EQUAL))
102:         {
103:           nxsched_switch(this_task(), tcb);
104:         }
105: #else
106:       FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
107: 
108:       if (rtcb->lockcount > 0)
109:         {
110:           /* Move all tasks with the higher or the same priority from
111:            * the ready-to-run list to the pending list.
112:            * If a running task has the same priority as other tasks on
113:            * the pending list, it must be executed last.
114:            */
115: 
116:           while (sched_priority <= nxttcb->sched_priority)
117:             {
118:               bool check = nxsched_remove_readytorun(nxttcb);
119:               DEBUGASSERT(check == false);
120:               UNUSED(check);
121: 
122:               nxsched_add_prioritized(nxttcb, list_pendingtasks());
123:               nxttcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_PENDING;
124: 
125:               nxttcb = tcb->flink;
126:             }
127: 
128:           /* Change the task priority */
129: 
130:           tcb->sched_priority = sched_priority;
131:         }
132:       else
133:         {
134:           /* A context switch will occur. */
135: 
136:           if (nxsched_reprioritize_rtr(tcb, sched_priority))
137:             {
138:               nxsched_switch(this_task(), rtcb);
139:             }
140:         }
141: #endif
142:     }
143: 
144:   /* Otherwise, we can just change priority since it has no effect */
145: 
146:   else
147:     {
148:       /* Change the task priority */
149: 
150:       tcb->sched_priority = sched_priority;
151:     }
152: }

108: /****************************************************************************
109:  * Name: nxsem_reset
110:  *
111:  * Description:
112:  *   Reset a semaphore count to a specific value.  This is similar to part
113:  *   of the operation of nxsem_init().  But nxsem_reset() may need to wake up
114:  *   tasks waiting on a count.  This kind of operation is sometimes required
115:  *   within the OS (only) for certain error handling conditions.
116:  *
117:  *   Mutex is simply posted until it is not blocking any tasks. If the
118:  *   requested count is 0, a single running holder is left. If the requested
119:  *   count is 1, the mutex is set to "reset". Other requested counts are not
120:  *   allowed for mutex.
121:  *
122:  * Input Parameters:
123:  *   sem   - Semaphore descriptor to be reset
124:  *   count - The requested semaphore count
125:  *
126:  * Returned Value:
127:  *   This is an internal OS interface, not available to applications, and
128:  *   hence follows the NuttX internal error return policy:  Zero (OK) is
129:  *   returned on success.  A negated errno value is returned on failure.
130:  *
131:  ****************************************************************************/
132: 
133: int nxsem_reset(FAR sem_t *sem, int16_t count)
134: {
135:   irqstate_t flags;
136: 
137:   DEBUGASSERT(sem != NULL && count >= 0);
138: 
139:   /* Don't allow any context switches that may result from the following
140:    * nxsem_post() operations.
141:    */
142: 
143:   sched_lock();
144: 
145:   /* Prevent any access to the semaphore by interrupt handlers while we are
146:    * performing this operation.
147:    */
148: 
149:   flags = enter_critical_section();
150: 
151:   if (NXSEM_IS_MUTEX(sem))
152:     {
153:       reset_mutex(sem, count);
154:     }
155:   else
156:     {
157:       reset_sem(sem, count);
158:     }
159: 
160:   /* Allow any pending context switches to occur now */
161: 
162:   leave_critical_section(flags);
163:   sched_unlock();
164:   return OK;
165: }

58: void nxsched_unlock(FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb)
59: {
60:   irqstate_t flags = enter_critical_section();
61:   FAR struct tcb_s *ptcb;
62: 
63:   /* In non-SMP:
64:    * If lockcount equals 0 and interrupts are not masked,
65:    * an interrupt may occur just before processing the g_pendingtasks queue,
66:    * causing the scheduler to switch to and start executing a lower-priority
67:    * task. At this moment, if there is a higher-priority task in the
68:    * g_pendingtasks queue, priority inversion will occur.
69:    */
70: 
71:   rtcb->lockcount = 0;
72: 
73:   /* Note that we no longer have pre-emption disabled. */
74: 
75:   if (!up_interrupt_context())
76:     {
77:       nxsched_critmon_preemption(rtcb, false, return_address(0));
78:       sched_note_preemption(rtcb, false);
79:     }
80: 
81:   /* Release any ready-to-run tasks that have collected in
82:    * g_pendingtasks.
83:    *
84:    * NOTE: This operation has a very high likelihood of causing
85:    * this task to be switched out!
86:    */
87: 
88: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
89:   ptcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_readytorun());
90:   if (ptcb && ptcb->sched_priority > rtcb->sched_priority &&
91:       nxsched_deliver_task(rtcb->cpu, rtcb->cpu, SWITCH_HIGHER))
92: #else
93:   ptcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_pendingtasks());
94:   if (ptcb && nxsched_merge_pending())
95: #endif
96:     {
97:       nxsched_switch(this_task(), rtcb);
98:     }
99: 
100: #if CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL > 0
101:   /* If (1) the task that was running supported round-robin
102:    * scheduling and (2) if its time slice has already expired, but
103:    * (3) it could not slice out because pre-emption was disabled,
104:    * then we need to swap the task out now and reassess the interval
105:    * timer for the next time slice.
106:    */
107: 
108:   if ((atomic_read(&rtcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_POLICY_MASK) ==
109:       TCB_FLAG_SCHED_RR && rtcb->timeslice == 0)
110:     {
111:       /* Yes.. that is the situation.  But one more thing.  The call
112:        * to nxsched_merge_pending() above may have actually replaced
113:        * the task at the head of the ready-to-run list.  In that
114:        * case, we need only to reset the timeslice value back to the
115:        * maximum.
116:        */
117: 
118:       if (rtcb != this_task())
119:         {
120:           rtcb->timeslice = MSEC2TICK(CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL);
121:         }
122: #  ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_TICKLESS
123:       else if ((atomic_or(&rtcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_PREEMPT_SCHED) &
124:                 TCB_FLAG_PREEMPT_SCHED) == 0)
125:         {
126:           nxsched_reassess_timer();
127:           atomic_and(&rtcb->flags, ~TCB_FLAG_PREEMPT_SCHED);
128:         }
129: #  endif
130:     }
131: #endif
132: 
133: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_SPORADIC
134: #  if CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL > 0
135:   else
136: #  endif
137:   /* If (1) the task that was running supported sporadic scheduling
138:    * and (2) if its budget slice has already expired, but (3) it
139:    * could not slice out because pre-emption was disabled, then we
140:    * need to swap the task out now and reassess the interval timer
141:    * for the next time slice.
142:    */
143: 
144:   if ((atomic_read(&rtcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_POLICY_MASK) ==
145:       TCB_FLAG_SCHED_SPORADIC && rtcb->timeslice < 0)
146:     {
147:       /* Yes.. that is the situation.  Force the low-priority state
148:        * now
149:        */
150: 
151:       nxsched_sporadic_lowpriority(rtcb);
152: 
153: #  ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_TICKLESS
154:       /* Make sure that the call to nxsched_merge_pending() did not
155:        * change the currently active task.
156:        */
157: 
158:       if (rtcb == this_task() &&
159:           (atomic_or(&rtcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_PREEMPT_SCHED) &
160:            TCB_FLAG_PREEMPT_SCHED) == 0)
161:         {
162:           nxsched_reassess_timer();
163:           atomic_and(&rtcb->flags, ~TCB_FLAG_PREEMPT_SCHED);
164:         }
165: #  endif
166:     }
167: #endif

173:  * Name:  sched_unlock

176:  *   This function decrements the preemption lock count.  Typically this
177:  *   is paired with sched_lock() and concludes a critical section of

201:     {
202:       nxsched_unlock(rtcb);
203:     }
